Special Tank.description:
• Mega Venusaur's respectable defensive stats, great typing, and access to the fantastic Thick Fat ability often make it a Mega Evolution of choice for bulky teams. It notably walls the most popular Primarina, Mega Lopunny, and Meowscarada sets; can stomach hits from powerful special attackers like Mega Gengar, Mega Charizard Y, and Archaludon; and provides utility with its immunity to Toxic against the likes of Umbreon, Toxapex, and Bellibolt.

  • Sludge Bomb: Sludge Bomb's decent chance to poison foes can punish defensive switch-ins and cripple bulky Pokemon that Mega Venusaur otherwise struggles to damage, like Umbreon, by chipping away at their health, especially when combined with the damage from Leech Seed.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power provides complementary coverage against the Poison- and Steel-types that Mega Venusaur's STAB attacks cannot hit well. For example, Earth Power will always 2HKO Archaludon.

  • Leech Seed: Leech Seed's healing can allow Mega Venusaur and potentially its teammates to remain healthy throughout the game; for example, a Timid Leech Seeded Mega Charizard Y has a very slim chance to 2HKO Mega Venusaur with Flamethrower in sun, giving it the opportunity to alternate between attacking and using Synthesis. Additionally, defensive Pokemon don't appreciate Leech Seed's chip damage, and it provides great insurance against Yawn cycling from Hippowdon and Umbreon by healing off some of the entry hazard damage taken by Mega Venusaur's teammates if it's forced to switch out to avoid falling asleep.

  • Giga Drain: At the cost of some of Leech Seed's more general utility, Giga Drain makes Mega Venusaur a bit more threatening to Ground-types like Hippowdon and Garchomp and Water-types like Mega Gyarados and Mega Blastoise. Though it does considerable damage to Basculegion-M, keep in mind that a 150-Base Power Last Respects 2HKOes Mega Venusaur even after Giga Drain's healing, meaning that this matchup is unfavorable for it unless Basculegion-M has already lost some HP.

  • Chlorophyll: While both of Venusaur's possible base abilities are very situational, Chlorophyll allows it to always outspeed and potentially revenge kill Mega Charizard Y in sun and is therefore generally preferred over Overgrow even on sets using Giga Drain.

  • Beware of Corviknight: Corviknight, as well as other slow and bulky pivots like Galarian Slowking to a lesser extent, is particularly annoying for Mega Venusaur because it can shrug off any attacks the Grass / Poison type throws at it and denies Leech Seed healing with U-turn. Mega Venusaur greatly appreciates teammates that can set hazards, such as Garchomp and Archaludon, to dissuade the opponent from repeatedly switching Corviknight in and out.

Other Options

  • Toxic: Though it's less useful against offensive teams than Leech Seed, stall teams can be devastated by a well-timed Toxic. If you elect to use Toxic, Sludge Wave may be preferable to Sludge Bomb to lessen the chance of Mega Venusaur inadvertently inflicting the weaker poison effect.

Other SP Spread

32 HP / 21 Def / 13 SpD with Bold: Mega Venusaur can run a physically defensive set, giving it a better matchup against Mega Lucario, Aegislash, and Swords Dance Garchomp at the cost of not being able to easily switch in on special attackers. With this spread, it avoids the 2HKO from Jolly Mega Lucario's Meteor Mash, and it has enough Special Defense to always survive Timid Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Overheat from full HP and avoid getting 2HKOed by Timid Mega Gengar's Sludge Wave.

Charizard.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Drought Offense.description:
• Drought turns Mega Charizard Y into one of the most ferocious wallbreakers in the game, as well as effective support against Water-types such as Primarina and Rotom-Wash!

  • Flamethrower versus Weather Ball: Flamethrower is Mega Charizard Y's most reliable Fire-type STAB move. Weather Ball offers a bit more power and gives Mega Charizard Y some extra coverage when the weather is changed, but this isn't always beneficial depending on the team you're facing.

  • Solar Beam: The blistering sun removes Solar Beam's biggest drawback, making it great coverage against common Water-types like Primarina and Rotom-Wash. Just be weary of weather changers like Hippowdon, Tyranitar, and Pelipper, which not only weaken Solar Beam's power but change it back to being a two-turn move!

  • Overheat: Overheat gets boosted to the heavens with the sunlight, with even Fire-resistant foes like Rotom-Wash and Garchomp taking over half their health from it! Just beware that the hit-and-run tactics Overheat encourages are heavily impacted by your opponent's team placing down Stealth Rock.

  • Flame Charge: Flame Charge transforms Mega Charizard Y into an effective late-game cleaner, with the bonus of destroying Focus Sash and Disguise.

  • Air Slash: Air Slash is a good secondary STAB move regardless of the current weather, especially against Mega Venusaur, whose Thick Fat can make it tricky to break through without risking an Overheat.

  • Timid versus Modest: Charizard is common enough where Speed ties can make or break games, but Modest does enhance Mega Charizard Y's wallbreaking power, with Overheat now having a small shot of OHKOing specially defensive Hippowdon.

  • Blaze versus Solar Power: Solar Power actually gives Charizard more power than its Mega Evolution, which can come in handy against opposing Mega Charizard Y teams. However, the damage it takes in the sun is unwelcome when Stealth Rock is in play, making Blaze the safer ability.

  • Sand Stream Partners: Since Mega Charizard Y relies on the warmth of the sun, resetting it with another weather ensures it keeps on roasting foes! Hippowdown is the star teammate here, having excellent defensive synergy with Mega Charizard Y and supporting it with Stealth Rock. Tyranitar doesn't work quite as well defensively, but it's still a worthy teammate as well thanks to its less predictable array of movesets.

  • Dealing with Stealth Rock: Mega Charizard Y should always run an odd HP stat to avoid getting 2HKOed by its archnemesis, Stealth Rock. Removing Stealth Rock is rather tricky in the current format, but if needed, Glimmora is the best Pokemon for that job with Mortal Spin, with the bonus of having Stealth Rock to further support Mega Charizard Y.

Other Options

  • Roost: While not a defensive Pokemon, Mega Charizard Y forces out enough Pokemon to justify using Roost. This can be especially helpful when Stealth Rock is up, giving Mega Charizard Y another chance to switch in.

  • Focus Blast: While not a reliable attack, Focus Blast deals massive damage to Tyranitar, which is otherwise one of Mega Charizard Y's strongest checks.

  • Dragon Pulse: Dragon Pulse is Mega Charizard Y's strongest attack against Dragon-types like Garchomp and Mega Dragonite, though note that Garchomp still takes massive damage from Fire-type attacks as long as the sun is shining.

  • Ancient Power: Ancient Power is a surprising attack to prevail in mirror matches against other Mega Charizard Y.

Dragon Dance.description:
• After a single Dragon Dance, Mega Charizard X can outspeed common metagame threats such as Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox and key Choice Scarf users such as Adamant Garchomp and Basculegion-M.

  • Roost vs. Coverage: Flare Blitz forces Mega Charizard X to take a lot of damage while attacking; Roost will allow Mega Charizard X to have more longevity and potentially allow for the option to set up more. Thunder Punch can be substituted in this slot if you are worried about Primarina, as at +1, it will OHKO maximum HP Primarina guaranteed. Earthquake is another coverage move to give Mega Charizard X the option to take on Tyranitar and Glimmora while at +1.

  • Adamant vs. Jolly: A Jolly nature gives +1 Mega Charizard X the Speed advantage versus foes like Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Adamant Garchomp as well as faster Mega Evolutions like Mega Gengar and Mega Greninja. Adamant cannot hit the same important Speed points, so can be used instead to bulk out Mega Charizard X to give it better opportunities to set up.

  • Possible Partner Pokemon: Mega Charizard X really does not enjoy facing down Glimmora, so having a reliable switch-in to its STAB options would go a long way. Hippowdon is a very strong option, as Hippowdon resists Glimmora's STAB moves and will provide Mega Charizard X with entry hazard support, allowing it to sweep more reliably. Other hazard setters like Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott can assist Mega Charizard X in getting OHKOs after a single boost.

Other Options

  • Outrage: Outrage can be used over Dragon Claw as a more oppressive option, but its move lock will limit Mega Charizard X's options in certain situations.

  • Scale Shot: Scale Shot is an interesting option over Dragon Claw that provides a better matchup against Garchomp, boosting Mega Charizard X's Speed further and getting around Focus Sash users. It, however, does not receive a boost from Tough Claws and can either miss or only hit twice, failing to get KOs.

  • Fire Punch: Fire Punch can be used over Flare Blitz if you want to maximize Mega Charizard X's longevity, but the drop in power will be significant.

SP Spreads

  • 12 HP / 29 Atk / 3 Def / 1 SpD / 21 Spe with Jolly: This spread is more optimized than just a basic 32/32/2 spread. The Speed investment allows Mega Charizard X to outspeed Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp after a Dragon Dance. The bulk investment will allow Mega Charizard X to survive Jolly Basculegion-M's 150-Base Power Last Respects guaranteed and Timid Mega Floette's Moonblast almost all of the time. An odd HP number will let Mega Charizard X switch in on Stealth Rock four times without fainting.

  • 16 HP / 30 Atk / 9 Def / 11 Spe with Adamant: This spread focuses more on Mega Charizard X's bulk than Speed while maximizing its damage output. After a Dragon Dance boost, Mega Charizard X will be able to OHKO maximum HP Mega Kangaskhan with Flare Blitz and OHKO maximum HP Archaludon sometimes, or guaranteed after a single layer of Spikes, with Flare Blitz. The HP and Defense investment lets Mega Charizard X tank a 150-Base Power Last Respects from Adamant Basculegion-M. 11 Speed SPs will allow Mega Charizard X to outspeed Mega Starmie and Adamant Choice Scarf Basculegion-M after a single Dragon Dance.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant or Jolly: If you're feeling uninspired, Mega Charizard X can run a basic offensive spread. An Adamant nature will allow for maximum power, but be aware that Mega Charizard X will miss important Speed benchmarks such as outrunning Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp. Jolly will provide Mega Charizard X with the Speed security, but it's worth knowing that beyond outspeeding Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp, there are not any significant Speed benchmarks unless your team is weak to Timid Choice Scarf Hydreigon.

Double Dance.description:
• Swords Dance will turn Mega Charizard X into a nuke with very few switch-ins. With access to Flame Charge and Scale Shot, Swords Dance Mega Charizard X can effectively run a set that will be difficult to stop.

  • Scale Shot vs. Flame Charge: Flame Charge is 100% accurate but significantly weaker, and it will lock Mega Charizard X out of coverage options if you run it alongside Flare Blitz. Scale Shot has the potential to be as powerful as Flare Blitz, but it can miss or only hit two or three times. It also does not get the Tough Claws boost, though after a single Swords Dance, a two-hit Scale Shot can knock uninvested Garchomp out.

  • Rounding Out the Set: Mega Charizard X doesn't need a lot of coverage when it has a +2 Attack boost. Roost will allow Mega Charizard X to use Flare Blitz multiple times and, in the right circumstances, set up further boosts. Dragon Claw can act as a more reliable STAB option for situations where Mega Charizard X doesn't want to risk using Scale Shot. Thunder Punch provides the coverage it needs to break through Primarina.

Other Options

  • Outrage: Outrage can be used as the third attack over a coverage move or Dragon Claw. It can provide Mega Charizard X the same massive damage output of Flare Blitz against Fire-resistant foes at the cost of being locked into the move.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake can be used as a strong neutral coverage option. It does not receive a boost from Tough Claws, but it can easily deal with Pokemon Mega Charizard X would otherwise not enjoy facing such as Tyranitar.

SP Spreads

  • 12 HP / 29 Atk / 3 Def / 1 SpD / 21 Spe with Jolly: The Speed allows Mega Charizard X to outspeed Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp after a Flame Charge or Scale Shot boost. The defensive investment will allow Mega Charizard X to survive 150-Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion-M and a Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette while having enough HP to allow Mega Charizard X to switch in on Stealth Rock four times.

  • 32 HP / 12 Atk / 3 Def / 1 SpD / 18 Spe with Adamant: Going Adamant will give Mega Charizard X a lot more bulk to play around with. This spread's bulk investment will allow Mega Charizard X to always survive Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake and Timid Glimmora's Power Gem. After a Speed boost from Scale Shot or Flame Charge, 18 Speed SPs will let Mega Charizard X outspeed Mega Lopunny. The Attack investment will let +2 Mega Charizard X knock out uninvested Garchomp with a two-hit Scale Shot.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant or Jolly: A simple offensive spread with either an Adamant or a Jolly nature can work, though it will lose out on important defensive calcs stated above. The leftover 2 SPs can be placed anywhere, but it should be noted that 2 or 0 HP SPs will leave Mega Charizard X with an odd HP number, letting it switch in on Stealth Rock four times.

Tank.description:
• By maximizing its physical bulk, Mega Charizard X can become a surprising answer to common Pokemon that would normally be expected to beat it one-on-one, such as Garchomp and Mega Starmie.

  • Dragon-type Move: Mega Charizard X can run a variety of viable Dragon-type moves on this set that all serve different functions. Dragon Tail will allow Mega Charizard X to act as a phazer and block foes' attempts to set up. Breaking Swipe will cripple almost all physical attackers, making them unable to break through Mega Charizard X. Dragon Claw is a good, reliable option if you are looking for consistent damage.

  • Flame Charge: Flame Charge will allow Mega Charizard X to more reliably take on common physical attackers such as Mega Starmie and Garchomp by allowing it to burn them with Will-O-Wisp before they can attack.

  • Possible Partner Pokemon: Tank Mega Charizard X will benefit from partners that can remove entry hazards or deter setup of them. Pokemon such as Meowscarada and Greninja will scare away common setters such as Garchomp and Hippowdon. Your own Garchomp or Hippowdon can scare away Glimmora while also providing Mega Charizard X with hazard support to complement burn damage and chip away at foes by phazing with Dragon Tail. Corviknight can Defog hazards away and protect Mega Charizard X.

Other Options

  • Flare Blitz: If you don't feel that the Speed security of Flame Charge is necessary for your team, Mega Charizard X can use other Fire-type STAB options. Flare Blitz will offer the highest damage but comes at the cost of Mega Charizard X's longevity.

  • Fire Punch: Fire Punch can be used over Flame Charge as a form of more reliable damage; it's not as powerful as Flare Blitz but does not have any major drawback.

SP Spreads

  • 30 HP / 29 Def / 7 Spe with Impish: This spread maximizes Mega Charizard X's physical bulk while running enough Speed to outspeed Mega Starmie and Sneasler after a single Flame Charge, letting it burn them with Will-O-Wisp before they can attack. The physical bulk investment lets it take on key threats such as Mega Starmie, Mega Kangaskhan, Garchomp, and Basculegion-M by being able to take a big hit, burn them, and then recover off the damage with Roost. The HP investment leaves Mega Charizard X with an odd HP number to maximize the number of times it can switch in with Stealth Rock up.

  • 26 HP / 29 Def / 11 Spe with Impish: Compared to the first one, this spread sacrifices a little bit of survivability in favor of outspeeding Adamant Basculegion-M. The HP stat remains an odd number to maximize the number of times Mega Charizard X can switch into Stealth Rock.

Half-Shell Hero (Shell Smash Sweeper).description:
• With an excellent typing and Shell Smash, Mega Blastoise is a potent and adaptable setup sweeper. If checks like Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Primarina are out of the way, Mega Blastoise's momentum can be difficult to stop!

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere is Mega Blastoise's most indispensable coverage option, allowing it to break through defensive mainstays Archaludon and Umbreon.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse puts the pressure on Mega Starmie and Basculegion-M, which can otherwise cut the momentum of a Mega Blastoise sweep short.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam may not benefit from Mega Launcher, but it's needed if you want Mega Blastoise to take on Mega Dragonite. It can also OHKO the ever-present Garchomp, as well as Hippowdon after a Shell Smash.

  • Water Pulse versus Hydro Pump: Water Pulse is the go-to STAB option thanks to Mega Launcher, and it's Mega Blastoise's best attack against threats like Mega Blaziken and Mega Mawile. Hydro Pump is less consistent then Water Pulse with only a small power increase, but the improved chance of OHKOing some Hippowdon without needing Shell Smash can make it worth the risk.

Other Options

  • White Herb: While the loss of Mega Launcher is a serious power drop, running White Herb can help Blastoise maintain its survivability while notably freeing up Mega Evolution for a teammate. Do note that Blastoise should be running Surf over Water Pulse due to the lack of Mega Launcher.

  • Water Spout: When Mega Blastoise is at full health, an unboosted Water Spout is a guaranteed OHKO on any variant of Hippowdon. In most other circumstances though, Blastoise is usually taking damage during Shell Smash setup, meaning that Water Spout will often be a worse option compared to Water Pulse or Hydro Pump.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 19 HP / 18 SpA / 29 Spe with Modest: This spread sacrifices some offensive power to let Mega Blastoise almost always avoid the 2HKO from Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake, which can be particularly important against Focus Sash leads. Enough Speed is maintained to outrun Jolly Choice Scarf Garchomp after a Shell Smash.

  • 11 HP / 29 SpA / 26 Spe with Modest: This spread is tuned towards Jolly Meowscarada, giving Mega Blastoise just enough bulk to always survive Flower Trick and almost always OHKO back with Ice Beam. Enough Speed is retained to outrun Timid Choice Scarf Hydreigon after a Shell Smash.

Turtle Power! (Bulky Attacker).description:
• Mega Blastoise packs high power upfront thanks to Mega Launcher. With a wide variety of coverage options, it can cause immediate havoc for opposing offensive teams!

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere helps Mega Blastoise trade effectively with all variants of Archaludon, in addition to 2HKOing physically defensive Umbreon and OHKOing maximum HP Hisuian Samurott.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse tips the Aegislash matchup into Mega Blastoise's favor and deals massive damage to Gholdengo and Mega Starmie.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam is necessary to deal any significant damage to Dragonite, and it's the best option against Garchomp and Meowscarada as well.

  • Water Pulse versus Hydro Pump: Water Pulse hits key targets like Hippowdon and Mega Blaziken hard and will also 2HKO maximum HP Mega Mawile. Hydro Pump trades the consistency of Water Pulse for a higher chance at OHKOing some Hippowdon.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet further cements Mega Blastoise's trading potential, letting it finish off weakened targets such as Focus Sash Garchomp and Sturdy Archaludon.

Other Options

  • Mirror Coat: Mirror Coat is an option for dealing with Primarina and Rotom-W, though be wary of Calm Mind Primarina.

The Rat (Paralysis Spreader).description:
• Mega Raichu Y is a fast but frail paralysis spreader that uses No Guard to fire off Zap Cannon and Focus Blast with perfect accuracy. Zap Cannon notably OHKOes bulky Primarina and severely dents Gholdengo while paralyzing most foes that survive, such as Mega Floette, often allowing Mega Raichu Y to outspeed and finish them off if they cannot KO it immediately. This makes Raichu difficult to revenge kill without a Ground-type or a faster attacker.

  • Focus Blast: Focus Blast covers Pokemon that resist Zap Cannon, OHKOing offensive Archaludon, Hydreigon, and Kingambit. However, specially defensive Archaludon, Rotom-Wash, and Garchomp can survive Focus Blast, so Mega Raichu Y or its teammates must weaken them first.

  • Grass Knot: Grass Knot prevents Ground-types from completely shutting down Mega Raichu Y; it notably OHKOes offensive Mega Swampert, has a good chance to OHKO physically defensive Hippowdon, and 2HKOes specially defensive Hippowdon.

  • Substitute versus Volt Switch: Substitute takes advantage of the switches Mega Raichu Y forces and works well with Zap Cannon's guaranteed paralysis; behind a Substitute, it can safely use Zap Cannon against faster foes such as Mega Delphox and Choice Scarf Hydreigon. If Hydreigon stays in to break the Substitute, Zap Cannon's paralysis will allow Mega Raichu Y to outspeed and KO it with Focus Blast, while switching risks getting Hydreigon's teammate paralyzed instead. Substitute also blocks priority moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and status moves such as Hippowdon's Yawn. Volt Switch lets Mega Raichu Y maintain momentum against switches it forces, but forgoing Substitute leaves it much more vulnerable to faster attackers and Choice Scarf users.

  • Mega Evolving Raichu: Raichu usually Mega Evolves immediately to gain No Guard and improved offensive stats. However, delaying Mega Evolution lets it absorb Electric-type attacks such as Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch and Archaludon's Electro Shot with Lightning Rod and gain a Special Attack boost, which is retained after Mega Evolving.

Other Options

  • Fake Out: Fake Out lets Mega Raichu Y provide immediate chip damage, notably breaking Focus Sash on common users such as Garchomp and Glimmora. It can also break Multiscale on Dragonite, letting Raichu or its teammates handle Dragonite more easily.

  • Alluring Voice: Alluring Voice gives Mega Raichu Y meaningful coverage against defensive Garchomp, which is immune to Zap Cannon and otherwise is usually 3HKOed by Focus Blast. It 2HKOes most non-Sitrus Berry Garchomp variants and deals considerably more damage than Focus Blast to specially defensive variants.

  • Encore: Encore punishes priority-based attempts to play around Mega Raichu Y, notably locking Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott into Sucker Punch or Aegislash into King's Shield. However, its usefulness is much more situational compared to Substitute, Volt Switch, or Fake Out.

Aurora Veil Support.description:
• Alolan Ninetales provides support in Aurora Veil and weather disruption, the former of which enables scary setup threats like Mega Gyarados, Mega Blaziken, and Mega Delphox. You can pair it with teammates like Aegislash and Gholdengo that can defensively switch into Steel-type threats like Mega Metagross and Archaludon.

  • Freeze-Dry: Freeze-Dry allows Alolan Ninetales to threaten Water-types like Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Mega Gyarados, and Primarina.

  • Blizzard versus Moonblast: Blizzard OHKOes Garchomp, heavily damages Hippowdon, and chunks offensive Archaludon sets that may switch into Alolan Ninetales. On the other hand, Moonblast lets Alolan Ninetales deal more damage to Mega Gyarados, Mega Blaziken, and Hisuian Samurott.

  • Encore: Encore disrupts opposing setup Pokemon like Swords Dance Mega Mawile, Calm Mind Mega Floette, and Iron Defense Corviknight, and it annoys defensive responses such as Defog Corviknight and Toxic Bellibolt.

SP Spreads

  • Alolan Ninetales prefers to have an even Defense stat, as it grants Alolan Ninetales one extra point of Defense when under snow.

  • 31 HP / 9 Def / 26 Spe with Bold: This spread allows Alolan Ninetales to generally survive Adamant Mega Metagross's Bullet Punch at full HP under snow, letting it set Aurora Veil for the team. The remaining SPs are invested in Speed, enabling Alolan Ninetales to outspeed Excadrill and Modest Mega Floette.

  • 31 HP / 3 Def / 32 Spe with Timid: Maximum SPs in Speed let Alolan Ninetales set Aurora Veil as early as possible, disrupt setup threats like Swords Dance Mimikyu with Encore, and outspeed and neutralize Garchomp. Near-maximum HP investment in tandem with snow lets it have a good chance to not get 2HKOed by +1 Mega Gyarados's Earthquake and OHKOed by +2 Garchomp's Earthquake, allowing it to set Aurora Veil or outright eliminate those threats. It also allows Alolan Ninetales to survive a Flash Cannon from Archaludon with Aurora Veil up, letting Alolan Ninetales come back later to set up snow or Aurora Veil.

  • 1 HP / 1 Def / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: A fully offensive SP spread lets Alolan Ninetales's Freeze-Dry have a good chance to OHKO Mega Swampert and guarantee an OHKO on offensive variants of Garchomp, and it also lets Moonblast OHKO offensive variants of Hisuian Samurott.

Focus Sash.description:
• Gengar's useful Speed tier, typing, and movepool give it a small niche as a Focus Sash user, disrupting setup sweepers with Destiny Bond. It can also trade with foes that often revenge kill it, such as Choice Scarf Garchomp and Mega Delphox.

  • Icy Wind: Icy Wind allows Gengar to threaten Dragonite and Garchomp while slowing down foes so it can reliably use Destiny Bond against them. However, Gengar should avoid using Icy Wind against Mega Staraptor, as it gains a Speed boost when hit by the move.

  • Destiny Bond: Destiny Bond lets Gengar force a lose-lose situation in a disadvantageous matchup, usually against setup sweepers trying to end games.

  • Focus Blast: Gengar can opt for Focus Blast to hit Kingambit and Tyranitar, two of the few Pokemon in the tier that resist its STAB combination. However, this comes at the price of unreliability.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt provides Gengar with coverage to hit foes such as Mega Gyarados and Pelipper, with the former usually resisting Shadow Ball.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp can neuter physically offensive foes such as non-Choice Scarf Garchomp, Kingambit, and Mega Staraptor, with the former two posing a threat to Gengar.

All-Out Attacker.description:
• Mega Kangashkan is the ultimate wild card and a frequent second option for Mega Evolution, as it is extremely adaptable when it comes to covering a team's weak spots.

  • Double-Edge versus Body Slam: Double-Edge exerts maximum pressure particularly on bulky checks that don't resist it, but the recoil can be problematic against faster, more offensive teams. Body Slam is much weaker but gives better balance between offense and survivability, and its paralysis chance synergizes excellently with Parental Bond.

  • Fake Out: With STAB and Parental Bond, Fake Out is a strong option for reliable priority and chip damage. Beware though, as it is easily predicted and can invite problematic checks in such as Stamina Archaludon and Flame Body Volcarona.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch is a more flexible priority option for Mega Kangashkan and is particularly threatening to Mega Gengar and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M.

  • Fire Punch: Fire Punch can turn the tables on Mega Scizor, which otherwise resists Mega Kangashkan's strongest moves. It also provides the best damage against Corviknight, though it fails to 2HKO physically defensive builds.

  • Ice Punch: Beyond dealing massive damage to Garchomp and Dragonite, Ice Punch getting two chances to freeze with Parental Bond can let Mega Kangashkan eke its way out of some dicey matchups.

  • Scrappy: Scrappy is the preferred ability prior to Mega Evolution, allowing Mega Kangashkan to get some quick free damage on Ghost-types with Fake Out. If it’s not using Fake Out, Inner Focus is a valid alternative but generally still not worth delaying Mega Evolution for.

Other Options

  • Facade: While highly situational, Facade can circumvent the problematic Flame Body Volcarona, turning a potential burn into a big power increase.

The Original Starwalker (All-out Attacke.description:
• Owing to its excellent Speed tier and immediately high damage output thanks to Huge Power, Mega Starmie is a threatening wallbreaker that is less reliant on setup than other physical Water-type attackers like Mega Gyarados and Mega Swampert. It does, however, have to deal with a low base HP and a weakness to common Choice Scarf users like Meowscarada, Hydreigon, and Basculegion-M, which leave it prone to being worn down and revenge killed.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet helps Mega Starmie pick off faster Pokemon, dealing significant damage to the threatening Mega Raichu Y, Mega Gengar, and Mega Blaziken. Having a priority attack also denies Sucker Punch from slower Pokemon like Kingambit, forcing the opponent to make awkward predictions.

  • Ice Spinner: Ice Spinner provides complementary coverage to Liquidation, super effectively hitting Dragon- and Grass-type Pokemon like Mega Dragonite and Mega Meganium. It will notably always OHKO even the most bulky of Garchomp.

  • Flip Turn: Thanks to Mega Starmie's high Speed, Flip Turn is a consistent pivoting option against Pokemon that defensively check it. Flip Turn additionally lets it deal chip damage while scouting for potential problematic coverage attacks like Thunder Punch from Mega Metagross. Against Pokemon that can run both offensive and defensive sets, Flip Turn can be useful to gauge damage while keeping Mega Starmie safe. For example, Liquidation will almost always OHKO offensive Mega Charizard Y in sun but cannot do the same to variants with HP investment, which can then punish Starmie for staying in by OHKOing it in return with Solar Beam.

  • Zen Headbutt: Zen Headbutt offers Mega Starmie a powerful option to neutrally hit Water-types it would otherwise struggle to damage, like Primarina and Rotom-Wash, and gives it a way to break the otherwise problematic Mega Venusaur and Toxapex. Electing to run Zen Headbutt over Ice Spinner will leave Mega Starmie with no good way to hit Hydreigon, however.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature helps Mega Starmie deal with Pokemon like Jolly Mega Metagross, letting it avoid Metagross's powerful attacks and do some chip damage with Flip Turn before Metagross is weak enough to be knocked out with Liquidation. Jolly additionally enables it to outspeed and potentially OHKO Mega Lucario and Mega Staraptor. An Adamant nature maximizes damage output, giving Ice Spinner an almost guaranteed chance to OHKO Hydreigon on the switch in and a decent chance to OHKO Mega Dragonite through Multiscale, and it still allows Mega Starmie to outpace Garchomp.

Other Options

  • Psycho Cut: Psycho Cut's higher accuracy when compared to Zen Headbutt makes it a bit more reliable, and with an Adamant nature, Mega Starmie retains a significant chance to OHKO specially defensive Mega Venusaur and Toxapex. However, Psycho Cut's lower power makes it difficult for even Adamant Mega Starmie to power through bulky Sitrus Berry variants of Rotom-Wash and Primarina.

Gyarados.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Sweeper.description:
• With Intimidate, Gyarados is able to set up, Mega Evolve, and sweep even under the pressure of physically offensive threats!

  • Waterfall: Even after a Dragon Dance, Mega Gyarados has just over a 50% chance to OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Waterfall under the sun!

  • Earthquake: An unboosted Earthquake is a reliable option for knocking out Mega Gengar with no HP investment and Mega Mawile. Earthquake also lets Mega Gyarados deal significant damage to Kingambit, Archaludon, and Mega Dragalage. Mega Gyarados is even capable of surviving Kingambit's STAB moves with two Supreme Overlord boosts! And thanks to Mold Breaker, it can also hit Levitate users such as Rotom-Wash, Rotom-Heat, and Mega Delphox.

  • Ice Fang: Ice Fang is extremely effective on Dragonite and Garchomp. It also covers Grass-types such as Mega Venusaur, Mega Meganium, and Meowscarada, which would otherwise be problematic for Mega Gyarados.

  • Crunch: Crunch can be used over Earthquake for landing a OHKO on Mega Gengar variants with maximum HP investment while covering Pokemon like Aegislash, the Basculegion-M, Mega Starmie, and Dragapult. After a Dragon Dance, Mega Gyarados manages to land a surprising OHKO on Shield forme Aegislash as long as it has no Defense investment! Keep in mind Crunch is a contact move, making Mega Gyarados susceptible to the Attack-lowering effect of King's Shield.

  • Power Whip: This is a situational and high-risk, high-reward option for Mega Gyarados to land an OHKO on opposing Mega Gyarados and Mega Swampert, as well as the bulkiest of Primarina and Rotom-Wash after a Dragon Dance.

  • Taunt: At the cost of dropping a coverage move, Taunt prevents defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon and Toxapex from healing themselves and disrupting Gyarados with Yawn and Haze, respectively. It also renders Corviknight incapable of using Iron Defense and Roost.

  • Mega Evolving Gyarados: It is recommended to wait until the right moment to Mega Evolve. This allows Gyarados to come into specific situations to create win conditions for itself. It's also important to note that non-Mega Gyarados and Mega Gyarados share the same Speed stat but have different typing and abilities; therefore, abstaining from Mega Evolving right away can be quite beneficial depending on the situation in question.

  • Before Mega Evolution: For example, Gyarados can switch in on a Choice-locked Earthquake from Garchomp in order to safely set up with Dragon Dance. It can also prevent Corviknight from using Iron Defense with Taunt while resisting Body Press and setting up additional Dragon Dances for a potential sweep. Finally, Gyarados's typing ensures that it won't be OHKOed by Mega Mawile's Play Rough.

  • After Mega Evolution: Mega Gyarados's Dark typing helps it resist Foul Play from Umbreon, Rotom-Wash, Rotom-Heat, and Archaludon, as well as Sucker Pucnh from targets like Mega Mawile and Kingambit. Mold Breaker also ignores various problematic abilities that can ruin its offensive momentum. Examples include Disguise from Mimikyu, Unaware from Skeledirge, and Levitate from Rotom-Wash and Rotom-Heat, with the last two being huge threats to Gyarados.

Abilities

  • Intimidate: This is the preferred option for cycling and safely setting up on physically offensive threats.

  • Moxie: Revenge killing a weakened and slower Pokemon with Moxie is an alternative for gaining an Attack boost before Mega Evolving.

SP Spreads

  • 1 HP / 32 Atk / 1 Def / 32 Spe with Jolly: This simple spread not only minimizes Stealth Rock damage but also lets Gyarados outspeed base 80 Speed Pokemon such as Mamoswine and non-Mega Dragonite. It also outspeeds Jolly or Timid Choice Scarf Basculegion-M after a Dragon Dance, and Swift Swim Mega Swampert after two uses of Dragon Dance.

Special Attacker.description:
• Mega Dragonite is a strong special attacker with endless coverage and Multiscale, which lets it trade well against offensive teams while being difficult to revenge kill at full health. Its ability to threaten Pokemon such as Corviknight, Garchomp, and Primarina without needing setup gives it immediate value over Dragon Dance variants.

  • Draco Meteor: Draco Meteor is Mega Dragonite's strongest attack, giving it immediate damage against neutral targets and Dragon-types such as Garchomp, Hydreigon, and opposing Mega Dragonite. Its Special Attack drop can make Mega Dragonite easier to take advantage of afterward, so it is best used when picking up a KO or forcing major damage on a key target.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt pressures Water- and Flying-types such as Primarina, Corviknight, Basculegion-M, and Mega Gyarados, preventing them from switching into Mega Dragonite safely.

  • Flamethrower versus Air Slash: Flamethrower is preferred for hitting Steel-types such as Aegislash, Kingambit, and Mega Scizor, which otherwise resist Draco Meteor and can take advantage of Mega Dragonite lacking Fire-type coverage. Air Slash is an alternative that gives Mega Dragonite a Flying-type STAB move to pressure Fighting- and Grass-types such as Mega Lopunny, Sneasler, Meowscarada, and Mega Venusaur.

  • Ice Beam versus Air Slash versus Roost: Ice Beam is preferred alongside Thunderbolt to give Mega Dragonite the coveted BoltBeam coverage, letting Mega Dragonite hit Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon, Garchomp, and opposing Mega Dragonite while also pressuring Mega Meganium. Air Slash can be used here if Mega Dragonite is already running Flamethrower but still wants a Flying-type STAB move. Roost trades coverage for longevity, letting Mega Dragonite preserve or reactivate Multiscale.

  • Modest versus Timid: A Modest nature maximizes Mega Dragonite's damage output while letting it outspeed positive-natured Archaludon, Rotom-Wash, Hisuian Samurott, and Ceruledge. A Timid nature trades power to make it outspeed faster positive-natured threats such as Hydreigon, Mimikyu, and Excadrill while Speed tying with positive-natured Charizard and Mega Kangaskhan.

Other Options

  • Hurricane versus Air Slash: Hurricane can be used over Air Slash for a stronger Flying-type STAB move, but its low accuracy makes it unreliable without rain support from Pelipper.

SP Spreads

  • 31 HP / 1 Def / 32 SpA / 1 Spe: This bulkier spread gives Mega Dragonite more opportunities to take advantage of Multiscale and trade hits with offensive Pokemon. However, the lack of Speed investment leaves it slower than threats the faster spread lets it outspeed, such as positive-natured Mega Gyarados, Mamoswine, Basculegion-M, and Mega Blastoise, so this spread should only be used when the extra bulk is more valuable than speed control.

Dragon Dance.description:
• Dragonite uses Multiscale to find setup opportunities with Dragon Dance, letting it become a threatening late-game sweeper with strong priority in Extreme Speed and the ability to break past common defensive Pokemon such as Toxapex and Aegislash with Earthquake.

  • Scale Shot versus Outrage: Scale Shot is preferred for boosting Dragonite's Speed further after Dragon Dance, making it harder to revenge kill without requiring multiple Dragon Dance boosts. Unlike Outrage, Scale Shot does not make contact, helping Dragonite avoid contact damage from Garchomp's Rough Skin. Outrage is a much stronger Dragon-type attack, but locking Dragonite into it can make it easier for Fairy-types like Primarina, Sylveon, and Mega Floette to punish it.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake gives Dragonite important coverage against Steel-, Fire-, Rock-, and Poison-types such as Aegislash, Kingambit, Mega Charizard X, Mega Tyranitar, and Toxapex.

  • Extreme Speed versus Roost: Extreme Speed gives Dragonite strong priority, letting it pick off weakened faster threats such as Sneasler, Mega Lopunny, and Greninja without relying on Scale Shot boosts. Roost is an alternative that helps Dragonite preserve Multiscale and set up more reliably against defensive Pokemon, but dropping Extreme Speed makes it easier to revenge kill.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: On Lum Berry sets, a Jolly nature lets Dragonite outspeed threats Adamant Dragonite cannot after Dragon Dance, such as Mega Gengar, Mega Delphox, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Greninja. An Adamant nature gives Dragonite more power while still outspeeding threats such as Meowscarada, Sneasler, Garchomp, and Hydreigon after a boost. On Dragoninite sets, Adamant Mega Dragonite already outspeeds the faster unboosted threats Jolly regular Dragonite aims for, while a Jolly nature improves Mega Dragonite's matchup against opposing boosted sweepers such as Adamant Scale Shot Garchomp, Dragon Dance Mega Tyranitar and Mega Charizard X, and Quiver Dance Volcarona.

Other Options

  • Thunder Punch: Thunder Punch lets Dragonite pressure Water- and Flying-types, such as Primarina, Azumarill, Corviknight, and Mega Clefable, but it is difficult to justify over Extreme Speed due to its revenge killing utility.

  • Fire Punch: Fire Punch can be used to hit Steel- and Grass-types such as Corviknight, Mega Scizor, Skarmory, and Mega Meganium more directly, but Earthquake is generally preferred for its stronger coverage.

Items

  • Lum Berry versus Dragoninite: Lum Berry gives Dragonite more freedom to set up through status from Pokemon such as Rotom-Wash, Umbreon, and Hippowdon. Dragoninite trades Dragonite's higher base Attack for Mega Dragonite's improved Speed tier, making it harder to revenge kill after a Dragon Dance.

Meganium.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Mega Meganium is able to leverage its high bulk and Special Attack to deal large amounts of damage while healing off incoming attacks with Synthesis bolstered by Mega Sol. It particularly is adept at threatening common defensive cores featuring the likes of Corviknight, Primarina, and Hippowdon.

  • Solar Beam: Mega Sol allows Mega Meganium to viably run Solar Beam, which fires off in a single turn to deal massive damage, notably OHKOes Primarina and Hippowdon, and ignores the latter's Sand Stream.

  • Weather Ball: Weather Ball is similarly enabled by Mega Sol, making it a potent coverage option that notably threatens Steel-types like Corviknight and Aegislash.

  • Dazzling Gleam: While it isn't the most powerful move, Dazzling Gleam gives Mega Meganium a crucial second STAB option that can threaten common Dragon-types that can otherwise take its Fire- and Grass-type moves such as Garchomp and Hydreigon, with the latter getting OHKOed.

Other Options

  • Earth Power: Earth Power can be used as an extra coverage option for Fire-types such as Ceruledge, which resist all of Mega Meganium's other attacks, as well as hitting Archaludon for super effective damage.

Umbreon.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

That's Amore! (Defensive Wish Passer).description:
• Owing to its high natural bulk, especially in a format without Assault Vest, Umbreon is able to carve out a role on bulky offense and stall teams as a Wish passer capable of taking on threats such as Dragapult, Hydreigon, and Mega Gengar.

  • Foul Play: Umbreon's most reliable attack, Foul Play heavily punishes physical setup sweepers that attempt to take advantage of its passivity. Because of Umbreon's low offensive stats, Foul Play typically does more damage against even special attackers than other options like Dark Pulse and Crunch.

  • Yawn: Yawn forces the opponent to either switch out their Pokemon, which gives Umbreon a free turn to benefit from Wish and Leftovers and can create an opening for one of Umbreon's teammates to come in, or let it stay in and stomach the sleep.

  • Wish + Protect: The combination of Wish and Protect gives Umbreon a consistent way to heal, letting it not only not have to worry about damage on the turn it uses Protect but also buy itself a turn for Leftovers recovery. The knowledge that Umbreon has Protect can also be used to bait your opponent into setting up on a turn they believe Umbreon will be inactive, allowing it to disrupt their Pokemon with Yawn.

  • Inner Focus versus Synchronize: While Synchronize is able to punish status spreaders like Rotom-Wash and defensive Dragapult, it comes with the detriment of potentially preventing Umbreon and its teammates from inflicting their own statuses. Inner Focus avoids this issue and allows Umbreon to consistently cycle Wish without having to worry about disruption from flinches.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt allows Umbreon to take on stall Pokemon such as Toxapex by removing their access to status and recovery moves. With 3 Stat Points invested in Speed, physically defensive Umbreon sets can outpace and duel with uninvested Corviknight, which can be a problem Pokemon for defensive teams, by denying it usage of Iron Defense and Roost.

  • Toxic: Giving up the utility of Yawn for the deadlier option in Toxic can allow Umbreon to wear down Pokemon it would otherwise struggle with, especially when Toxic is combined with Protect. Passive teammates that can't use Toxic themselves also appreciate the damage Umbreon provides.

  • Baton Pass: Though Umbreon is not typically passing stat boosts, Baton Pass can still be useful as a slow pivoting option to bring in a weakened teammate that needs to be healed with Wish. It also gives Umbreon a way to escape from Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag if need be.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is Umbreon's most generally useful item, providing it with passive healing and reducing its reliance on Wish to stay healthy.

  • Mental Herb: Mental Herb is an alternative defensive item that prevents Taunt users from denying Umbreon the use of Wish, which can be crucial late-game. Mental Herb also allows Umbreon a little more consistency against Encore users it is otherwise unthreatened by like Skeledirge.

  • Chople Berry: Chople Berry improves Umbreon's matchups against a few Pokemon that run Fighting-type coverage, such as Focus Blast Mega Gengar and Close Combat Aegislash. It can, in return, 2HKO and OHKO these Pokemon with Foul Play, respectively.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpD with Bold vs. 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpD with Calm: Umbreon can succeed with investment in either of its defenses, which depends on the needs of its team. Physical sets do better against the likes of Kingambit and Dragon Darts Dragapult, while special sets do better against Pokemon like Mega Gengar and Hydreigon.

Scizor.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Swords Dance.description:
• Scizor serves as an excellent revenge killer within the tier thanks to its powerful STAB priority Bullet Punch, enabling it to clean up against weakened foes and Fairy-types such as Mega Lopunny, Mega Gengar, and Sylveon.

  • Scizorite versus Lum Berry: Scizor is versatile enough that it can forgo its Mega Stone to allow for a different Mega Evolution on the team, while Scizor uses Lum Berry to switch into Yawn from Sylveon and Hippowdon safely and set up a free Swords Dance. However, Mega Scizor is a significant improvement over Scizor, as it can always OHKO Archaludon with Close Combat after a Swords Dance.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat can allow for Scizor to majorly threaten Corviknight after a Swords Dance and potentially OHKO Archaludon.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off lets Scizor handle Aegislash and deals with Mega Delphox as it tries to switch in.

  • U-turn: U-turn allows Scizor to do respectable damage as it pivots out of foes that can handle it, such as Umbreon.

  • Roost: Roost enables Scizor to recover as it sets up against threats unable to reliably threaten it, such as Mega Venusaur, Meowscarada, and Sylveon.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can be used on non-Scizorite sets, granting Scizor recovery when not running Roost.

Special Wall.description:
• Tyranitar uses Sand Stream, excellent special bulk, and Stealth Rock to function as a special wall that can check attackers such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Gengar, and Mega Delphox while making progress with item removal and chip damage.

  • Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock helps punish common switch-ins and breaks Focus Sash, which is especially valuable against offensive Pokemon such as Sneasler, Meowscarada, and Ceruledge. It also pressures Pokemon weak to Rock, such as Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona.

  • Knock Off versus Foul Play: Knock Off gives Tyranitar a consistent way to make progress by removing items from switch-ins such as Corviknight, Hippowdon, and Rotom-Wash. Foul Play is an alternative that punishes physical attackers and setup sweepers such as Dragonite, Mega Charizard X, and Garchomp without requiring much Attack investment.

  • Rock Blast versus Rock Tomb: Rock Blast gives Tyranitar a multi-hit Rock-type attack that can break Substitute and pressure Dragonite through Multiscale while still threatening targets such as Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona. Rock Tomb is a weaker alternative, but its Speed drop can punish switch-ins and allow Tyranitar or its teammates to more easily outspeed foes.

  • Earthquake versus Ice Punch: Earthquake gives Tyranitar coverage for grounded Steel- and Rock-types such as Kingambit, Archaludon, and opposing Tyranitar, especially when catching them on the switch. Ice Punch instead targets Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon and Garchomp, which can otherwise take advantage of Tyranitar.

  • Rest: Rest can be used over coverage to give Tyranitar more longevity. However, dropping Earthquake leaves Tyranitar unable to reliably pressure Kingambit and Archaludon, while dropping Ice Punch makes Garchomp and Hippowdon much safer switch-ins.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry gives Tyranitar general recovery, helping it stay healthy enough to set Stealth Rock and continue checking special attackers throughout a game.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry should be used with Rest, letting Tyranitar fully heal once without being forced to stay asleep afterward.

  • Shuca Berry: Shuca Berry fits best on Ice Punch sets, letting Tyranitar survive physical Ground-type attacks from Pokemon such as Garchomp and punish them in return.

Setup Sweeper.description:
• Mega Tyranitar uses its excellent bulk, Sand Stream-boosted Special Defense, and Dragon Dance to turn forced switches and favorable trades into setup opportunities. This lets it set up or trade against special attackers it threatens, such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Delphox, Mega Gengar, Volcarona, and even would-be checks like Primarina, which can be forced to respect a boosted Stone Edge.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off is Mega Tyranitar's most consistent Dark-type STAB move, letting it heavily pressure Pokemon such as Aegislash, Mega Gengar, and Mega Delphox while removing items from defensive switch-ins like Corviknight, Hippowdon, and Primarina.

  • Stone Edge: Stone Edge gives Mega Tyranitar a strong Rock-type STAB move to OHKO Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Volcarona, Pelipper, Gyarados, and Dragonite with prior sand chip damage.

  • Ice Punch versus Fire Punch: Ice Punch is preferred for hitting Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon and Garchomp, which can otherwise stomach Mega Tyranitar's STAB attacks. Fire Punch is an alternative for pressuring Steel-types such as Corviknight, Mega Scizor, and Kingambit more directly, though it leaves Mega Tyranitar worse off against common Ground-types.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature gives Mega Tyranitar better Speed after Dragon Dance, letting it outspeed threats such as Mega Gengar, Meowscarada, and Sneasler after a boost. An Adamant nature gives Mega Tyranitar more immediate power while still letting it outspeed threats such as Garchomp, Mega Floette, and Gengar after a Dragon Dance.

Other SP Spread

  • 26 HP / 16 Atk / 1 SpD / 23 Spe with Adamant or Jolly: This bulkier spread lets Mega Tyranitar survive Meowscarada's Flower Trick, Corviknight's Body Press, and Garchomp's Earthquake, giving it more setup opportunities against these threats. Mega Tyranitar's Speed is kept high enough to outspeed uninvested Mega Venusaur and Mega Meganium before boosting. After a Dragon Dance, Adamant Mega Tyranitar still outspeeds positive-natured Garchomp, Mega Floette, and base 100s such as Mega Charizard X, Mega Charizard Y, and Volcarona. A Jolly nature can be used instead to outspeed Gengar and Mega Lucario after a Dragon Dance, though the lower Attack investment and nature make Mega Tyranitar noticeably weaker.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Mega Tyranitar uses its excellent bulk, Sand Stream, and immediate power to pressure bulkier teams without needing Dragon Dance; it uses Knock Off and coverage to punish defensive Pokemon such as Corviknight, Skarmory, Hippowdon, and Mega Meganium.

  • Rock Blast versus Stone Edge: Rock Blast trades raw power for better accuracy and multi-hit utility, letting Mega Tyranitar break Substitute and Focus Sash while pressuring Dragonite through Multiscale. Stone Edge maximizes Mega Tyranitar's immediate Rock-type damage, making it better for punishing neutral targets and bulky switch-ins.

  • Ice Punch versus Fire Punch: Ice Punch hits Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon, Garchomp, and Hydreigon. Fire Punch is an alternative that pressures Steel-types such as Corviknight, Mega Scizor, Skarmory, and Kingambit more directly.

  • Superpower: Superpower lets Mega Tyranitar hit Dark- and Steel-types such as Umbreon, Kingambit, opposing Tyranitar, and Archaludon.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt can be used to stop defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon, Hippowdon, Skeledirge, and Corviknight from using Yawn, Will-O-Wisp, recovery, and phazing moves. Taunt pairs especially well with Superpower against Umbreon, since Superpower is Mega Tyranitar's strongest move against it but can be stalled out by Wish and Protect. However, fitting Taunt usually means dropping Ice Punch, Fire Punch, or a STAB move, making Mega Tyranitar easier for Ground-types, Steel-types, and Fairy-types to handle, respectively.

Other SP Spread

  • 32 HP / 20 Atk / 14 SpD with Adamant: This spread keeps Mega Tyranitar bulky while still letting it hit hard, as the extra Special Defense investment lets it almost always survive Timid Mega Gengar's Focus Blast at full HP while sand is active. The drop in Attack is noticeable compared to maximum Attack variants, but the improved Mega Gengar matchup can justify the trade-off.

Rain Sweeper.description:
Swampert is a deadly sweeper on rain teams with Pelipper, being able to outspeed a vast portion of the metagame and OHKO targets that do not resist Water with its massive Attack stat while keeping up momentum with Flip Turn. It also has good matchups against metagame staples Mega Metagross and Archaludon. Despite its incredible Speed in rain, it is still slower than certain threats like Choice Scarf Meowscarada and can be threatened by other weather users like Mega Charizard Y.

  • Wave Crash: Wave Crash hits incredibly hard in rain, dealing massive damage even to Water-resistant foes like Hydreigon, Greninja, Primarina, and Meowscarada, making it difficult for them to switch in.

  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch provides coverage against Dragon- and Grass-types like Garchomp, Mega Dragonite, Hydreigon, and Mega Meganium while avoiding further recoil damage from Wave Crash.

  • Flip Turn: Flip Turn is useful for pivoting out against walls like Mega Meganium as well as wearing down checks such as Choice Scarf Meowscarada, Rotom-Wash, Alolan Ninetales, and Gyarados.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant provides a useful damage boost and can OHKO Mega Charizard Y as it switches in and sets sun or Mega Staraptor with HP investment in rain. Jolly allows Swampert to outspeed common Choice Scarf users like Hydreigon and Adamant Meowscarada, as well as sweepers like Mega Charizard X, Volcarona, and Dragonite at +1 while rain is active.

Other Options

  • Bulk Up: Bulk Up provides Swampert with a way of breaking through Pokemon it struggles with like Mega Gyarados, though this uses precious rain turns and will not have much use when facing other weather users like Mega Charizard Y or Alolan Ninetales.

  • Rain Dance: Swampert can manually set rain when it cannot rely on Pelipper, though it will not last as long due to Swampert's inability to hold Damp Rock.

  • Substitute: Substitute is an option against foes trying to switch into Swampert's STAB attacks, forcing them to either stay in to remove it or switch out and let a teammate take the hit instead. This is particularly useful against Choice Scarf Meowscarada trying to switch in, as it risks being KOed by Adamant Ice Punch.

Rain Support.description:
• Pelipper is the main facilitator of rain teams, often preferred over fellow Drizzle user Politoed thanks to its Flying typing. It pairs excellently with Mega Swampert and Archaludon, which can take advantage of rain with Swift Swim and Electro Shot. The three also cover for each other's weaknesses, as Pelipper appreciates the two for being able to switch in on Electric-type attacks like Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon, while Archaludon appreciates Pelipper for being a switch-in to Hippowdon's Earthquake with its Ground-type immunity.

  • U-turn: U-turn provides Pelipper with a safe way of bringing in Mega Swampert, Basculegion-M, and Archaludon, since they usually want to maximize their turns in the rain. It can also break Focus Sash in the process of doing so. U-turn allows Pelipper to gain momentum against threats that change the weather such as Alolan Ninetales and Mega Charizard Y. This makes resetting the weather back to rain much easier, as all Pelipper has to do is switch in again. Furthermore, U-turn is helpful for providing momentum against counters like Rotom-Wash.

  • Weather Ball vs. Surf: Weather Ball is generally preferred due to its higher Base Power in the rain. Surf can be used to let Pelipper punish Alolan Ninetales, Hippowdon, and Mega Charizard Y for switching in without risking a Hurricane miss. With Surf, it also does not have to worry about rain running out of turns.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam targets Garchomp and hits Archaludon neutrally. It provides coverage against Dragon- and Flying-types in the scenario where rain might not be up, but it only does slightly more damage than Hurricane even against super effective targets.

Other Options

  • Roost: Pelipper will sometimes want to use Roost with more defensive sets. This allows it to heal up on Meowscarada, Hippowdon, or even Mega Swampert, granting it better longevity as a physical wall.

  • Tailwind: Tailwind can be very helpful for Archaludon and its middling Speed stat by turning it into a potent sweeper. Other teammates like Mega Metagross and Mimikyu can benefit from it, too.

Items

  • Damp Rock: Damp Rock allows Pelipper to have a longer effect on the battle long after it's left the field, making rain turns harder for opposing players to stall out.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash provides survivability against Electric-type attacks like Zap Cannon from Mega Raichu Y and Thunder Punch from Mega Metagross and Mega Blaziken, as well as strong special attacks like Draco Meteor from Archaludon. This allows Pelipper to get an attack in and still be able to switch in later.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpD with Relaxed: This spread emphasizes Pelipper's physical bulk; it improves Pelipper's matchup against Triple Axel Meowscarada and Rock Slide Garchomp by making their attacks 3HKOs rather than 2HKOs. The Relaxed nature simultaneously makes it a slower pivot than Corviknight and Scizor.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest: 32 Speed SPs allow Pelipper to outspeed most Primarina, Kingambit, and opposing uninvested Pelipper. A Modest nature boosts Pelipper's damage, notably allowing for a guaranteed 3HKO on Mega Gyarados with Hurricane and an OHKO on Mega Raichu Y with Weather Ball. It also helps against Mega Venusaur, which Pelipper's teammates tend to struggle with.

Swords Dance.description:
• Mega Mawile uses its key defensive typing, massive Attack, and impressive bulk to take on important metagame threats such as Archaludon, Mimikyu, Meowscarada, and non-Earthquake Mega Metagross. It can also threaten foes like Basculegion-M, Mega Gyarados, and Primarina with its strong attacks.

  • Play Rough Play Rough is Mega Mawile's primary STAB move and the move that it will be using most of the time. It allows Mega Mawile to rip through Mega Gyarados and physically defensive variants of Umbreon, OHKOing the former even if Mawile was affected by Intimidate and having a high chance to OHKO the latter.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch gives Mega Mawile a way to finish off weakened foes like Mimikyu and Garchomp. It also targets Fairy-resistant Dark-weak foes, namely Aegislash, Mega Gengar, and Mega Metagross.

  • Fire Fang vs. Thunder Punch: Despite being weak, Fire Fang deals with nasty Steel-types like Aegislash, Gholdengo, Kingambit, Scizor, and opposing Mega Mawile, which can shrug off Mega Mawile's STAB moves. Alternatively, Thunder Punch is stronger and can be used instead to hit the likes of Corviknight, Pelipper, Primarina, and Hisuian Samurott. While Thunder Punch is weaker than Play Rough against Mega Staraptor, it is the more consistent option.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head gives Mega Mawile a reliable secondary STAB move to smack Mega Floette, always OHKOing even Calm Mind variants that have a significant investment in Defense.

  • Adamant vs. Brave: An Adamant nature gives Mega Mawile the maximum damage output it needs. However, a Brave nature can instead be used to outspeed Bellibolt and Mega Dragalge in Trick Room while keeping the power boost from Adamant.

  • Mega Evolving Mawile: Mawile is able to cycle Intimidate before it Mega Evolves, allowing it to safely set up with Swords Dance against physically offensive foes. Because of Mega Staraptor's Contrary ability, Mawile's Intimidate will rather increase its Attack, ensuring that Blaze Kick can OHKO Mega Mawile with enough chip damage. Therefore, Mega Evolving Mawile right away when Mega Staraptor isn't on the field can ensure that this situation is avoided.

Offensive.description:
• Mega Metagross is one of the strongest Mega Evolutions in Regulation M-B. Its excellent power, solid natural bulk, great defensive typing, and bevy of coverage options make it a juggernaut capable of winning one-on-one matchups against most relevant Pokemon.

  • Psychic Fangs: Beyond being its most reliable STAB move, Psychic Fangs's effect improves Mega Metagross's good matchups versus dual screens setters like Alolan Ninetales and Grimmsnarl.

  • Bullet Punch: Bullet Punch OHKOes uninvested Mimikyu after Disguise is broken and uninvested Alolan Ninetales in snow, and it can also finish off quicker Focus Sash users and faster foes that are at low health. If Mega Metagross is going to be sacrificed, it can use Bullet Punch to chip a foe into KO range of its teammates' attacks.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake heavily damages Steel-types like opposing Mega Metagross, Archaludon, and Gholdengo.

  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch OHKOes any Garchomp without heavy bulk investment. Additionally, it KOes Dragonite after Multiscale is broken and can give Mega Metagross a fighting chance against Hydreigon.

  • Thunder Punch: Thunder Punch usually OHKOes Mega Charizard Y, and it also 2HKOes Mega Gyarados and physically defensive Primarina.

  • Mega Evolving Metagross: It's best to Mega Evolve Metagross as soon as possible, though Clear Body prevents Gyarados from weakening Metagross with Intimidate and stops Grimmsnarl from pivoting out with Parting Shot.

Other Options

  • Hammer Arm: Hammer Arm OHKOes Kingambit, Hydreigon, and Hisuian Samurott in addition to 2HKOing Umbreon and maximum HP Archaludon, though the Speed drop will make Mega Metagross easy to revenge kill.

  • Grass Knot: Even with no Special Attack investment and a hindering nature, Grass Knot 2HKOes physically defensive Hippowdon and is likely to OHKO Mega Swampert, though it doesn't offer much useful coverage beyond that.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head is capable of OHKOing bulky Fairy-types like Sylveon and Mega Floette. However, the main STAB options offer useful utility that's hard to pass up for Iron Head, and replacing a coverage move leaves Mega Metagross less well-rounded in its matchups.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant or Jolly: Aside from making Mega Metagross hit harder in general, an Adamant nature guarantees the OHKO on Mega Charizard Y and Mega Lucario with Thunder Punch and Earthquake, respectively. It also makes Ice Punch likely to OHKO physically defensive Garchomp. A Jolly nature lets Mega Metagross always outspeed Alolan Ninetales and Adamant Meowscarada; additionally, Jolly ensures that it outspeeds and 2HKOes opposing uninvested Adamant Mega Metagross with Earthquake.

  • 20 HP / 21 Atk / 25 Spe with Jolly: Sacrificing some power or Speed for bulk can help Mega Metagross secure matchups against specific Pokemon. This spread is tailored against Garchomp; Mega Metagross outspeeds Jolly variants and is bulky enough to usually survive Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake after taking Rough Skin damage.

  • 8 HP / 32 Atk / 1 Def / 25 Spe with Adamant: This spread retains maximum offensive investment while giving Mega Metagross enough bulk to withstand Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake after Rough Skin damage most of the time, as well as letting it avoid the OHKO from Hydreigon's Dark Pulse. The Speed investment allows it to outspeed Adamant Garchomp.

Mega Contrary.description:
• Mega Staraptor is a threatening offensive Mega Evolution in Regulation M-B thanks to its excellent stats, near-unresisted offensive typing, and ability to threaten such foes like Archaludon and Volcarona.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat gives Mega Staraptor a way to boost its defenses. Close Combat also lets it pick off weakened foes while hitting Flying-resistant foes like Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Mega Lucario, in addition to making them excellent starting points for gaining boosts. With these boosts, it becomes very hard to take down.

  • Brave Bird: Mega Staraptor uses its strong STAB Brave Bird to threaten Fighting-resistant or -immune foes such as Mega Delphox, Mega Charizard Y, Basculegion-M, and Mimikyu.

  • Roost: Roost provides Mega Staraptor a consistent way to heal and gives it incredible longevity when combined with boosts from Contrary Close Combat.

  • Blaze Kick: While its offensive typing is excellent, Mega Staraptor can run Blaze Kick to tear down Aegislash and Gholdengo, both of which would otherwise wall its attacks. Also, Aegislash has trouble using King's Shield in this matchup, as King's Shield boosts Mega Staraptor's Attack instead of lowering it.

  • Substitute: Substitute is a way for Mega Staraptor to avoid status-inflicting moves like Mortal Spin from Glimmora and Yawn from Hippowdon. It also lets Mega Staraptor set up more easily while taking advantage of passive Pokemon such as Hippowdon.

  • U-turn: U-turn makes Mega Staraptor a hit-and-run attacker, giving its team momentum while chipping common switch-ins such as Aegislash, Gholdengo, and Mega Floette. It also breaks Mimikyu's Disguise; while Brave Bird and Blaze Kick also break Disguise, U-turn lets Mega Staraptor pivot to another teammate, like Archaludon, to deal with Mimikyu.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Maximizing Attack and Speed lets Mega Staraptor strike hard and go first as much as possible.

  • 31 HP / 3 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: A bulky spread allows Mega Staraptor to become even harder to take down, ensuring that it can survive a Psyshock from Timid Mega Delphox.

All-out Attacker.description:
• Mega Lopunny's excellent Speed and Attack make it one of the best Mega Evolution choices and premier cleaners, further bolstered by Scrappy nullifying Intimidate from foes such as Gyarados eliminating the need for Mega Lopunny to have coverage against Ghost-types.

  • Fake Out: Thanks to Scrappy, Mega Lopunny's Fake Out is a powerful tool, providing guaranteed chip damage and allowing Mega Lopunny to finish off weakened sweepers like Mega Gyarados and Volcarona.

  • Triple Axel: Triple Axel allows Mega Lopunny to reliably threaten various Dragon-types such as Garchomp and Dragonite, even getting around Focus Sash and Multiscale, respectively, thanks to its multiple hits.

  • U-turn: With U-turn, Mega Lopunny can adopt a hit-and-run playstyle that makes great use of its high Speed and immediate threat level, weaving in and out of battle and picking off foes when it finds an opening.

Other Options

  • Thunder Punch: Thunder Punch can be useful for picking off weakened Corviknight and Primarina; however, losing the coverage of Triple Axel can hurt Mega Lopunny's ability to threaten potentially more important targets like Garchomp.

  • Mach Punch and Quick Attack: Mach Punch and Quick Attack fill a similar role to Fake Out, giving Mega Lopunny a strong priority option to pick off weakened foes. However, these trade Fake Out's guaranteed chip damage for more flexibility thanks to not being restricted to use on the first turn Mega Lopunny is on the field.

Swords Dance.description:
• With Swords Dance, Mega Lopunny can punish defensive play by boosting its Attack to terrifying levels and clean up weakened teams with ease thanks to its incredible Speed.

  • Fake Out vs. Mach Punch: Fake Out is still very useful on a Swords Dance set, allowing Mega Lopunny to get guaranteed damage on foes and finish off weakened sweepers. Mach Punch gives Mega Lopunny more flexibility in cleaning up weakened teams, as it can outspeed other priority users like Mega Lucario and Kingambit with a boosted Mach Punch.

  • Triple Axel: Triple Axel is Mega Lopunny's best option for breaking through foes like Garchomp, Dragonite, and Hippowdon.

  • Facade: Facade gives Mega Lopunny more freedom in setting up Swords Dance, as it no longer fears being burned. A status-boosted Facade from +2 Mega Lopunny can prove extremely difficult for even the bulkiest teams to withstand.

Other Options

  • Encore: Encore allows Mega Lopunny to create its own setup opportunities by locking foes into moves such as Stealth Rock and Recover.

  • Thunder Punch: Thunder Punch allows Mega Lopunny to more reliably threaten Corviknight and Primarina.

Garchomp.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Offensive Stealth Rock.description:
• Garchomp's excellent Speed tier and power make it one of the premier offensive choices for setting up Stealth Rock.

  • Outrage: Despite this set usually being used early-game to set up Stealth Rock, Outrage still gives Garchomp good cleaning potential and makes it a decent revenge killer if Focus Sash is still intact.

  • Rock Tomb versus Poison Jab: Rock Tomb is a perfect fit for the early-game playstyle of this set, ensuring foes like Mega Gyarados and Dragonite won't be able to set up Dragon Dance freely after Garchomp's Focus Sash is broken, in addition to being a great response to both Mega Charizard formes.

  • Focus Sash: Despite Garchomp's above average bulk, its sheer prominence means enough Pokemon are aiming to OHKO it, which makes Focus Sash worth using for the more reliable Stealth Rock setup.

Other Options

  • Poison Jab: If Mega Meganium is a serious issue for your team, Poison Jab can potentially flip that matchup.

  • Dragon Tail: While usually better sorted towards more defensive Garchomp sets, Dragon Tail still has merit due to preventing bulky Steel-types like Iron Defense Corviknight and Swords Dance Mega Scizor from setting up.

Swords Dance.description:
• Garchomp's good bulk and coverage place it near the top of the food chain of Swords Dance sweepers!

  • Scale Shot: Scale Shot's reliability issues and reduction of Garchomp's bulk may make it seem like a strange choice for a sweeper, but the Speed boost makes Garchomp so much harder to revenge kill that it's worth it overall.

  • Poison Jab versus Fire Fang: Poison Jab punctures through Mega Meganium, which otherwise can wall and revenge kill Garchomp fairly easily, as well as dealing with the rare Mega Clefable. Fire Fang, however weak it may be, is Garchomp's best shot of chewing through a weakened Corviknight, which otherwise is a strong Garchomp check.

Other Options

  • Outrage: Outrage makes Garchomp very vulnerable to being revenge killed, but its perfect accuracy and sheer power make it worth considering. Outrage pairs especially well with Lum Berry to cure confusion and block Yawn from Hippowdon, which is almost always 2HKOed by boosted Outrage even when it chomps down on a Sitrus Berry!

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash severely punishes teams that are unable to set up Stealth Rock, in addition to enhancing Garchomp's revenge killing capabilities. The vulnerability to entry hazards does sometimes conflict with this set's preference for late-game sweeping, though.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry is an excellent response to common status users like Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash, leaving even less defensive answers for Garchomp.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb gives Garchomp a tremendous power boost, now being able to OHKO offensive Mega Metagross without a boost! This comes at the cost of the recoil making Garchomp more vulnerable to priority attacks.

  • Haban Berry: Choice Scarf Dragon-types such as opposing Garchomp and Hydreigon are common enough where Haban Berry can be useful to put less pressure on boosting Speed with Scale Shot.

  • Roseli Berry: Roseli Berry can be a deadly surprise for Fairy-types like Mimikyu and bulky Primarina that are expecting to revenge kill Garchomp.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Garchomp's impressive power, Speed, and bulk make it arguably among the apex Choice Scarf revenge killers of Pokemon Champions Singles!

  • Outrage: While locking Garchomp into a Rampaging state makes it easy prey for Fairy-types like Primarina and Mimikyu, the power Outrage offers turns Garchomp into a ferocious late-game cleaner and an effective revenge killer of most Dragon-type foes.

  • Poison Jab: Poison Jab is Garchomp's preferred Fairy-type deterrent, OHKOing offensive Mega Meganium after Stealth Rock and usually 2HKOing the rare Mega Clefable as well.

  • Rock Tomb versus Dragon Claw: Rock Tomb not only OHKOes Mega Charizard Y but also ensures that fast setup sweepers that may come in after the KO such as Dragon Dance Dragonite and opposing Swords Dance Garchomp will be easier to revenge kill thanks to the Speed drop. Dragon Claw, on the other hand, is Garchomp's most reliable Dragon-type STAB move, perfect for revenge killing weakened Dragon-types without fearing the wrath of Fairy-types getting a free KO.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: Opposing Choice Scarf Garchomp are common enough that Jolly is the safer nature to use; Jolly also lets Garchomp outspeed Jolly Mega Dragonite. However, Adamant's power boost does make Garchomp a better late-game cleaner, granting it a good chance of OHKOing Mega Delphox with Outrage for example.

Other Options

  • Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock may seem nonsensical on a revenge killer, but it does give Garchomp some early-game utility if fitting in a more dedicated Stealth Rock setter is difficult for your team, at the cost of some revenge killing prowess. It also can be used to fool your opponent into thinking this set doesn't have Choice Scarf.

  • Rock Slide: While it offers less utility than Rock Tomb, Rock Slide's flinch chance has the potential to flip a bad matchup.

  • Iron Head: Poison Jab is usually preferred due to OHKOing Mega Meganium, but Iron Head's flinch chance could flip matchups against Fairy-types Garchomp can't OHKO, such as Mega Clefable, Mega Floette, and Sylveon. Additionally, Iron Head KOes Mimikyu after Disguise is broken without Stealth Rock support.

Chonky Chomp (Phazer).description:
• Garchomp uses its fantastic bulk to inflict double trouble, placing entry hazards and using Dragon Tail to disrupt and rack up damage on opposing teams.

  • Spikes: Combining Spikes with Stealth Rock can make it much harder for defensive staples like Hippowdon to stay healthy throughout a match.

  • Rock Slide: Even without Attack investment, Rock Slide is still strong enough to OHKO offensive Mega Charizard Y.

  • SP Spread: The given SP spread has enough physical bulk to avoid the OHKO from opposing Jolly Garchomp's Outrage as well as Mega Kangaskhan's Ice Punch if using Sitrus Berry. The special bulk investment allows Garchomp to dodge the OHKO from Modest Primarina's Moonblast and Mega Gengar's Icy Wind. The leftover SPs are put into Speed.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst recovery helps Garchomp stay healthy and continue to be a nuisance. Particularly after big attacks like Primarina's Moonblast, Garchomp can heal out of range of a follow-up Aqua Jet.

  • Haban Berry: Haban Berry is the most reliable method of letting Garchomp tank Draco Meteor from the likes of Archaludon and Hydreigon.

Swords Dance.description:
• Mega Lucario is a nearly unwallable breaker, threatening physical walls like Hippowdon after a Swords Dance and minimal chip. Mega Lucario also has access to priority moves that prevent faster threats like Mega Raichu Y from revenge killing it and an above-average Speed tier that lets it outpace Mega Metagross and Garchomp, making it a great late-game cleaner. However, Mega Lucario struggles to find openings to set up without taking too much damage, cannot deal with certain Ghost- and Water-types like Aegislash and Toxapex, and falls short of OHKOing physically defensive Mega Venusaur and Hippowdon. Alolan Ninetales can provide Mega Lucario with Aurora Veil, while pivots like Rotom-Wash and Choice Scarf Meowscarada can help it find more opportunities to set up. Alternative Mega Evolutions that deal with Aegislash, like Mega Gyarados and Mega Delphox, also pair well with Mega Lucario, as do teammates that provide entry hazard support like Hippowdon and Garchomp.

  • Swords Dance: Swords Dance gives Mega Lucario the power it needs to pummel bulky walls like Corviknight and Rotom-Wash.

  • Meteor Mash versus Earthquake: Meteor Mash breaks through Fairy-types like Primarina and Mega Meganium. It also gives Mega Lucario a chance to gain an additional Attack boost, which would let it outright OHKO physically defensive Mega Venusaur with Meteor Mash at +3. Alternatively, Earthquake allows Mega Lucario to power through Ceruledge and Aegislash.

  • Extreme Speed versus Bullet Punch: At +2, Extreme Speed OHKOes offensive Mega Raichu Y and picks off faster Pokemon that resist Steel, like Mega Greninja and Mega Blaziken. However, Bullet Punch can be considered to threaten Mega Gengar and Mimikyu.

  • Mega Evolving Lucario: Lucario should usually Mega Evolve as soon as possible unless it expects Gyarados or Staraptor to come in and neutralize its Swords Dance boost, as Inner Focus prevents Intimidate from affecting it. With Intimidate blocked, Lucario can Mega Evolve the next turn and OHKO them with Close Combat and Meteor Mash, respectively.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Maximum Attack and Speed investment with a Jolly nature lets Mega Lucario outspeed and deal with Mega Metagross, Mega Staraptor, and Alolan Ninetales.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: An Adamant nature gives Mega Lucario a better chance to OHKO Hippowdon and Mega Venusaur at +2 after Stealth Rock damage. It also makes Mega Lucario's priority moves more threatening, allowing it to OHKO offensive checks like Choice Scarf Hydreigon, Mega Delphox, and Mega Gengar at +2 after minimal chip.
