However, Mega Lucario will be slower than Mega Metagross, Garchomp, and Mega Charizard Y.

Special Sweeper.description:
• Nasty Plot Mega Lucario is a deadly setup sweeper that can be hard to prepare for, ripping down weakened teams with its STAB moves, high Special Attack, Adaptability, and good offensive and defensive typing. With these traits, it can become very difficult to stop once checks such as Skeledirge and Toxapex have been removed.

  • Nasty Plot: Nasty Plot gives Mega Lucario more power, ensuring that it can OHKO bulky Pokemon like Rotom-Wash.

  • Aura Sphere: This is Mega Lucario's primary STAB move, ensuring that it gets a small chance to OHKO specially defensive Corviknight with +2 Aura Sphere after Stealth Rock damage.

  • Flash Cannon: Flash Cannon serves as Mega Lucario's main way of hitting Fairy-type foes like Mimikyu and Mega Floette for super effective damage. With this, it can also guarantee an OHKO on the latter after Stealth Rock damage.

  • Vacuum Wave: Vacuum Wave is useful for picking off weakened metagame threats such as Hydreigon and Mega Lopunny. It also has a high chance to OHKO Meowscarada after Stealth Rock chip damage.

Other Options

  • Steel Beam: Mega Lucario can opt for Steel Beam to deal bigger damage to Fighting-resistant or -immune foes like Mimikyu. However, the move's extreme recoil results in Flash Cannon being the overall better STAB move.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse can catch Aegislash, Gholdengo, and Mega Starmie off-guard, as these three resist both of Mega Lucario's STAB moves. However, Dark Pulse has poor coverage aside from that, and its STAB moves are generally better against most of the metagame.

Hippowdon.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Stealth Rock.description:
• With impressive bulk, a great defensive typing, and a useful ability that wears foes down, Hippowdon is the premier setter of Stealth Rock!

  • Yawn: Yawn is the secret ingredient to Hippowdon's success, punishing sweepers that lack Lum Berry such as Iron Defense Mega Metagross and working well with Stealth Rock to rack up even more residual damage with switches.

  • Slack Off versus Whirlwind: Slack Off would normally be a given on such a defensive Pokemon, but Hippowdon can justify going without it to cause even more Stealth Rock damage with Whirlwind. Whirlwind also punishes Pokemon that may run Lum Berry to set up on Hippowdon, such as Garchomp and Kingambit.

Other Options

  • Rock Tomb: Not only does Rock Tomb provide utility in Speed reduction against common Ground-type switch-ins like Gyarados, but it also ensures that Hippowdon isn't totally walled by Flying-types.

  • Protect: Protect pairs well with Yawn and Leftovers, potentially letting Hippowdon incapacitate switch-ins that can otherwise threaten to seriously harm it such as Meowscarada and Hydreigon while also providing a small serving of free recovery.

  • Fissure: When your back is up against a wall, Fissure could potentially flip matchups by OHKOing switch-ins Hippowdon has no business beating, such as Mega Meganium. However, its low reliability makes it hard to fit in compared to Whirlwind.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's quick burst of recovery usually fits Hippowdon the best, giving it a chance to let loose a Yawn more easily. It also helps specially defensive variants deal with White Herb Archaludon.

  • Leftovers: If Sitrus Berry is held by another teammate, Leftovers's slower recovery still benefits Hippowdon, especially variants that run Slack Off.

  • Mental Herb: If both Sitrus Berry and Leftovers are needed on other teammates, Mental Herb can be justified for letting Hippowdon set up Stealth Rock even when hit by Taunt. It can be particularly helpful in preventing Taunt Mega Gyarados from easily setting up.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpD with Impish: Maximizing Hippowdon's tanky Defense stat gives it the best chance of stopping powerful physical sweepers like Garchomp late-game with Yawn or Whirlwind.

  • 32 HP / 5 Def / 29 SpD with Careful: This specially defensive spread lets Hippowdon survive Primarina's Mystic Water-boosted Sparking Aria.

  • 32 HP / 10 Def / 24 SpD with Careful: This spread should be paired with Sitrus Berry, as it allows Hippowdon to avoid a 2HKO from White Herb Archaludon's Draco Meteor while also surviving Garchomp's +2 Outrage after Stealth Rock damage.

  • 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpD with Careful: Maximizing Hippowdon's Special Defense gives it a good shot of avoiding an OHKO from Modest Mega Charizard Y's Overheat in the sun.

Curly Brace's Machine Gun (Offensive).description:
• Mamoswine shows off its offensive face-to-face capabilities against a wide array of targets, including powerhouse Pokemon like Garchomp and Mega Dragonite! It also carves a niche as the only Stealth Rock user in the format with Oblivious, which allows it to safely set entry hazards without worrying about getting Taunted!

  • Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock breaks Garchomp's and Meowscarada's Focus Sash and Dragonite's Multiscale. Other relevant targets that can have their survivability severely compromised by Stealth Rock include Volcarona and Charizard.

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb provides speed control against faster foes and will always OHKO Mega Charizard Y. The Speed drop becomes particularly useful for aiding an ally Choice Scarf user like Garchomp or Meowscarada to move before their counterparts.

  • Icicle Spear: If Mamoswine is used as a lead or an early-game attacker and there's no opportunity for it or an ally to set Stealth Rock in order to attempt to break a foe's Focus Sash, Icicle Spear is the best option to take on these users. A two-hit Icicle Spear will always OHKO Garchomp, and three hits OHKO Protean Meowscarada as long as it retains its Grass typing. Three hits also OHKO Dragonite, even with Multiscale. Another noteworthy target is Mimikyu, as the first hit can get around Disguise. However, OHKOing Mimikyu often requires a total of four or five hits with high damage rolls.

  • Icicle Crash: Despite the shaky accuracy compared to Icicle Spear's, the power of Icicle Crash is not conditioned by a total number of hits. Thus, it can deliver reliably high amounts of damage, potentially 3HKOing physically defensive Hippowdon after Sitrus Berry recovery. The moderate flinch chance can also potentially buy extra turns for Mamoswine against a slower foe.

  • Ice Shard: Ice Shard allows Mamoswine to pick up KOs and revenge kill Choice Scarf users like Garchomp, Meowscarada, and Hydreigon. Preserving Mamoswine after it's used its Focus Sash can also be valuable late-game for picking up a KO against the aforementioned foes. Ice Shard also takes out faster Pokemon that do not use or learn priority moves, such as Garchomp and Hydreigon. Ice Shard can also take care of Mega Mawile and Kingambit if they're put in KO range with Earthquake.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake can potentially OHKO Mega Mawile and also covers various relevant Pokemon like Mega Raichu Y, Mega Metagross, Aegislash, Archaludon, Kingambit, and Bellibolt.

  • Watch Out for Glimmora and Archaludon: Toxic Debris Glimmora can potentially switch in on Icicle Spear and set two layers of Toxic Spikes in the process. Meanwhile, Stamina Archaludon can switch in and snowball with a Defense boost per each successive hit, which makes it significantly harder to deal with.

Other Options

  • Freeze-Dry: If a rain archetype is particularly troublesome when leading, Freeze-Dry can be used to significantly damage Pelipper and Mega Swampert.

  • Endeavor: At low HP, Endeavor can make muscling through a more resilient Pokemon easier for Mamoswine or its teammates.

Abilities

  • Oblivious: Oblivious ensures Mamoswine is not affected by Mawile's and Gyarados's Intimidate. It also blocks Taunt so that Mamoswine can safely set up Stealth Rock.

  • Thick Fat: With Thick Fat, Mamoswine becomes capable of surviving a +2 Torch Song from Skeledirge. It can even survive the combination of Flamethrower and Extreme Speed from Modest Mega Dragonite after taking Stealth Rock damage!

Rotom-Heat.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Offensive Pivot.description:
• With a Choice Scarf, Rotom-Heat becomes a speedy pivot and disruptor. Levitate also lets Rotom-Heat switch in on Pokemon that often use Ground-type attacks such as Choice-locked Garchomp, Mega Metagross, and Mega Venusaur, and revenge kill them if they're weakened enough.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge: Thunderbolt is preferred for higher damage. Discharge can be used instead for the higher chance of paralysis.

  • Volt Switch: This turns Rotom-Heat into an offensive pivot, allowing it to leave matchups where it can't do much damage and safely bring another teammate in the process.

  • Overheat: This is the best and only option for Rotom-Heat to threaten Meowscarada and Scizor. If Rotom-Heat is using a Modest nature, Overheat has a very high chance to OHKO Mega Meganium with maximum HP investment and also deals massive damage to specially defensive Corviknight, but it narrowly misses a chance to land the OHKO even with Stealth Rock damage. In the event Mega Meganium and Corviknight survive, they can use their recovery moves to offset the damage they receive as Rotom-Heat's Special Attack decreases with every use of Overheat, so this should only be used to pick up the KO if they're weakened enough.

  • Trick: Even though Choice Scarf is a highly coveted item for speed control, Trick can be used to lock a defensive Pokemon into a move and make it virtually useless for the rest of the battle.

  • Modest versus Timid: On one hand, a Modest nature allows Rotom-Heat's Thunderbolt to have a very low chance to OHKO Mega Charizard Y, as well as 2HKOing specially defensive Corviknight after Leftovers recovery. On the other hand, a Timid nature can be used for outspeeding Jolly Gyarados that has used Dragon Dance.

Rotom-Wash.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Pivot.description:
• The combination of an excellent defensive typing, fantastic ability, and solid bulk lets Rotom-Wash act as a great pivot that can handle physical attackers such as Garchomp, Dragonite, Mega Gyarados, and Scizor.

  • Volt Switch: Volt Switch lets Rotom-Wash maintain momentum, allowing its teammates to get on the field safely.

  • Hydro Pump: Hydro Pump gives Rotom-Wash reliable damage against the Ground-types that try to switch into Volt Switch.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp acts as a deterrent for physically offensive foes, such as Sneasler, Dragon Dance Dragonite, Aegislash, and Garchomp.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge: Thunderbolt has more Base Power than Discharge, but Discharge can be used to paralyze foes faster than Rotom-Wash, such as Mega Lopunny, Sneasler, and Greninja.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry provides quick healing to Rotom-Wash, especially after surviving high-Base Power moves from strong foes.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers can be used as an alternative option over Sitrus Berry, providing Rotom-Wash passive healing, which makes up for its lack of reliable recovery. Additionally, Leftovers synergizes with a Bold nature and the secondary stat spread better than Sitrus Berry.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 SpA / 2 Spe with Modest: Maximizing Rotom-Wash's decent Special Attack stat allows it to roll a very small OHKO chance on Mega Charizard Y, as well as letting Rotom-Wash reliably 2HKO Dragonite after Stealth Rock and specially defensive Hippowdon.

  • 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpA with Bold: When fully invested in Defense, Rotom-Wash can stop powerful physical sweepers, such as Garchomp and Kingambit, while threatening them with Will-O-Wisp.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf turns Rotom-Wash into a fast pivot and revenge killer, letting it outspeed key threats such as Charizard, Mega Lopunny, and Garchomp.

  • Volt Switch: Volt Switch lets Rotom-Wash take advantage of its Choice Scarf by dealing chip damage to faster threats such as Mega Gengar and Sneasler before pivoting into a teammate that can handle them. It also helps Rotom-Wash keep momentum against Pokemon it forces out, such as Corviknight and Mega Charizard Y.

  • Trick: Trick lets Rotom-Wash cripple defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon and Hippowdon by locking them into one move, making it easier for teammates to take advantage of them.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge: Thunderbolt gives Rotom-Wash a stronger Electric-type attack when it does not want to pivot out with Volt Switch, notably helping against Primarina, Corviknight, and Mega Gyarados. Discharge trades power for a higher paralysis chance, which can punish switch-ins and support slower teammates.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp gives Rotom-Wash a way to punish physical attackers such as Garchomp, Kingambit, and Mega Scizor. However, it is harder to justify than an Electric-type attack because Rotom-Wash usually needs to use Trick first, as being locked into Will-O-Wisp can leave it easy to take advantage of.

Samurott-Hisui.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Offensive Spikes Setter.description:
• Hisuian Samurott serves an important role in the metagame as an excellent lead and the tier's premier Spikes setter through Ceaseless Edge while also being able to threaten the likes of Mega Metagross, Hippowdon, and Gholdengo with its good movepool.

  • Sacred Sword: Sacred Sword lets Hisuian Samurott chunk opposing Dark-types such as Mega Gyarados and Hydreigon along with ignoring Archaludon's Stamina Defense boosts.

  • Razor Shell vs. Aqua Cutter: Although the choice is mostly your preference, Razor Shell hits a bit harder, notably always 2HKOing physically defensive Hippowdon and potentially 2HKOing Mega Scizor with a Defense drop. Aqua Cutter is, however, perfectly accurate, making it a safer cleanup tool.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch can pick off weakened or faster targets such as Garchomp, Mega Delphox, and Basculegion-M.

  • Flip Turn: Flip Turn can be used to pivot out and keep up momentum should Hisuian Samurott be up against problematic walls like Primarina and Mega Meganium.

  • Encore: Encore can punish more passive options like Corviknight's Roost or Umbreon's Wish, allowing Hisuian Samurott to freely slice away at them.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This is a basic spread that lets Hisuian Samurott hit hard and move quickly.

  • 14 HP / 32 Atk / 8 SpD / 12 Spe with Jolly: This spread will let Hisuian Samurott nearly always survive Modest Archaludon's Draco Meteor while outspeeding bulkier Mimikyu sets.

Items

  • Black Glasses: Black Glasses increases the power of Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge and Sucker Punch. It allows the former to potentially OHKO Shield forme Aegislash and Mega Metagross, while the latter will always OHKO uninvested Basculegion-M and nearly always OHKO Mega Starmie.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash allows Hisuian Samurott to work as an incredible lead, usually enabling at least a layer of Spikes to be set up, and it can allow Hisuian Samurott to successfully trade against opposing leads such as Glimmora.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott provides excellent role compression through speed control and entry hazard support from Ceaseless Edge. It can remove threats such as Mega Starmie, Mega Delphox, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M.

  • Ceaseless Edge: Ceaseless Edge sets entry hazards, lets Hisuian Samurott generate progress against bulkier teams, and breaks opposing Pokemon's Focus Sash. It also lets Hisuian Samurott deal with Mega Gengar and Gholdengo. However, Hisuian Samurott is unable to beat Aegislash one-on-one from full HP because King's Shield lowers its Attack.

  • Sacred Sword: Sacred Sword cuts through Mega Lucario and Mega Lopunny. Hisuian Samurott is OHKOed from full HP by +2 Mach Punch from Mega Lopunny but not by +2 Vacuum Wave from Mega Lucario. It also ignores Defense boosts, which allows Hisuian Samurott to finish off Archaludon in a pinch.

  • Flip Turn: Flip Turn preserves momentum for Hisuian Samurott's teammates by allowing it to switch out of checks like Corviknight, Primarina, and Toxapex. It also deals some chip damage to Mega Metagross, allowing Hisuian Samurott to OHKO it later with Ceaseless Edge.

  • Razor Shell versus Aqua Cutter: Razor Shell gives Hisuian Samurott a chance to break through physically defensive Hippowdon with a Sitrus Berry over two turns if it lowers Hippowdon's Defense. It also guarantees an OHKO on offensive Mega Raichu Y. On the other hand, Aqua Cutter has perfect accuracy at the cost of slightly less power. Either move OHKOes Mega Delphox and all except the bulkiest variants of Volcarona.

  • Potential Partners: Hisuian Samurott is relatively weak and not that fast even with a Choice Scarf, leaving it unable to OHKO threats such as Mega Gyarados and Mega Metagross or outspeed +1 Mega Blaziken; teammates that can reliably handle these threats, such as Garchomp and Mega Blaziken, are greatly appreciated. Pokemon like Mega Gengar and Swords Dance Scizor that benefit from Hisuian Samurott's pivoting capabilities also make for great teammates.

SP Spreads

========

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Maximum Attack and Speed investment with a Jolly nature lets Hisuian Samurott outspeed +1 Mega Gyarados and fast threats like Mega Greninja and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: An Adamant nature may be considered, as it allows Hisuian Samurott to guarantee an OHKO on Mega Raichu Y with Aqua Cutter and plausibly 2HKO Corviknight on the switch if Razor Shell lowers Corviknight's Defense. However, the reduced Speed means Hisuian Samurott Speed ties with Mega Lopunny and is outsped by +1 Mega Gyarados, though it can still outspeed and remove Mega Delphox.

• Choice Scarf Hydreigon serves as a solid speed control option and revenge killer for teams, being able to outspeed and remove the likes of Mega Gengar, Ceruledge, and non-Choice Scarf Garchomp.

  • U-turn: U-turn enables Hydreigon to keep up momentum against switch-ins it cannot threaten, such as Sylveon and Primarina.

  • Flamethrower: Flamethrower allows Hydreigon to threaten foes such as Mega Meganium, Scizor, and Kingambit.

  • Timid Timid enables Hydreigon to outspeed threats such as Choice Scarf Adamant Garchomp and Adamant Mega Charizard X after a Dragon Dance.

Other Options

Natures

-Modest: Modest lets Hydreigon always OHKO Mega Starmie and gives it a much better chance to OHKO Basculegion outright.

Offensive.description:
• Hydreigon can serve as a pivotal offensive piece for teams using its high Special Attack and solid natural Speed. Its good typing and ability enable it to safely come in against the likes of Hippowdon and Ceruledge, then proceed to break apart the opposition.

  • Flamethrower can help Hydreigon break through the likes of Corviknight and Scizor.

  • U-turn: U-turn enables Hydreigon to keep up momentum against checks such as Primarina and Sylveon.

  • Taunt: Taunt can shut down the likes of Hippowdon and Umbreon, preventing them from forcing Hydreigon out with tools like Yawn.

  • Nasty Plot: Nasty Plot enables Hydreigon to threaten OHKOs on foes such as Mega Venusaur with Draco Meteor.

  • Modest: With a Modest nature, Hydreigon can threaten an OHKO on specially defensive targets like Hippowdon and Corviknight after a Nasty Plot boost with Draco Meteor and Flamethrower, respectively.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash allows Hydreigon to trade against threats such as Sneasler and Mega Starmie with Draco Meteor and Dark Pulse, respectively.

  • White Herb: White Herb enables Hydreigon to fire off two full-power Draco Meteors in a row, potentially overwhelming a would-be check such as Umbreon.

  • Lum Berry: With a Lum Berry, Hydreigon can safely switch into Hippowdon or Umbreon going for Yawn and set up a Nasty Plot in their face.

Other Options

Natures

  • Timid: A Timid nature enables Hydreigon to outspeed threats such as Jolly Mimikyu and prevents a Speed tie with Timid Archaludon and Jolly Ceruledge.

Delphox.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Crimson Maiden (Offensive Mega).description:
• Mega Delphox works as an excellent wallbreaker, with its blazing base 134 Speed and strong STAB combination enabling it to outspeed and handle threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Charizard Y, and Corviknight without much issue.

  • Psychic-type STAB Moves: For its secondary STAB move, Mega Delphox has plenty of choice options. Psychic does the overall highest damage, allowing Mega Delphox to 2HKO Hippowdon and OHKO Mega Venusaur after Stealth Rock. However, Psyshock deals with more specially bulky targets like Primarina, while Psychic Noise can bypass the Substitute Mega Gengar loves to hide behind.

  • Dazzling Gleam: If you're looking for coverage, Dazzling Gleam serves as Mega Delphox's best option to handle pesky Dark-types such as Hydreigon and Umbreon.

  • Encore: Encore serves as Delphox's premier utility option; it locks foes such as Kingambit and Sneasler into options like Sucker Punch and Swords Dance, allowing Mega Delphox to set up a Substitute or Nasty Plot safely.

  • Nasty Plot: Nasty Plot can turn Mega Delphox's already powerful moves into immense bombs, enabling Mega Delphox to OHKO foes such as Garchomp with Psychic.

  • Substitute: Substitute can punish threats incapable of hurting Mega Delphox like Corviknight and Sylveon, allowing it to stay in on foes such as Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Mega Lopunny that could threaten it out otherwise, and can help it out against Sucker Punch users such as Kingambit and Focus Sash Meowscarada.

Other Options

  • Focus Blast: If you wish to go gambling on unreliable moves, Focus Blast serves as a much cleaner check to Dark-types overall compared to Dazzling Gleam, notably OHKOing Tyranitar and 2HKOing Umbreon.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: A very basic and standard spread, it leaves Mega Delphox lacking any real bulk but lets Mega Delphox just hit hard and fast.

  • 1 HP / 4 Def / 29 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: An overall bulkier spread that, at the cost of a small bit of damage output, grants Mega Delphox a nearly guaranteed chance to survive Choice Scarf Garchomp's Outrage.

Torrent Focus Sash.description:
• Focus Sash guarantees Greninja survives any single attack, allowing it to reliably reach the HP range needed to activate Torrent, which boosts its Water-type attacks to trade damage or secure KOs against foes it would otherwise struggle against.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse is Greninja's most reliable STAB move, pressuring Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Mega Delphox, Basculegion-M, Mega Gengar, Aegislash, and Ceruledge. Its decent flinch chance is useful after Focus Sash activates to potentially prevent Greninja from being KOed.

  • Surf versus Hydro Pump: Surf provides accurate and consistent damage against targets like Hippowdon and Glimmora. Hydro Pump is much stronger, allowing Greninja to secure crucial KOs on bulky checks like Tyranitar and Corviknight that Surf fails to pick up, though its low accuracy makes it less reliable.

  • Water Shuriken: Water Shuriken becomes incredibly threatening when boosted by Torrent, allowing Greninja to pick off faster threats that have been brought down to their Focus Sash such as Meowscarada and Sneasler.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam is crucial coverage for heavily damaging Dragon- and Ground-types such as Dragonite and Garchomp.

  • Toxic Spikes versus Taunt versus Counter: Toxic Spikes wears down checks like Umbreon and Primarina over time. Taunt shuts down defensive Pokemon like Corviknight and prevents Glimmora from setting entry hazards up. Counter allows Greninja to heavily punish physical attackers, notably securing an OHKO against Meowscarada from the lead position.

  • Modest versus Timid: A Modest nature is preferred because Focus Sash guarantees Greninja survives hits from faster attackers, which makes the extra damage output for Torrent-boosted attacks more valuable. Even without a Speed-boosting nature, Modest Greninja outspeeds Jolly Garchomp, Timid Mega Charizard Y, and Jolly Mega Kangaskhan. A Timid nature can be used to outspeed faster threats such as Adamant Meowscarada, Jolly Mega Lucario, and Sneasler.

Other Options

  • Sludge Wave: Sludge Wave can be used to hit Fairy-types such as Primarina, Mega Meganium, and Clefable, but without Protean's STAB boost and defensive type change, it is generally less justifiable for this set over other coverage options.

Protean Focus Sash.description:
• Focus Sash ensures Greninja avoids being OHKOed; this ensures it can utilize Protean to defensively pivot or offensively retaliate with STAB-boosted moves.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam is mandatory, as it provides excellent coverage for OHKOing Dragon-types like Garchomp and Mega Dragonite.

  • Sludge Wave: Sludge Wave pressures Fairy- and Grass-types such as Primarina, Mega Floette, and Meganium, with Protean also changing Greninja's typing to Poison to resist their attacks.

  • Mud Shot: Mud Shot is the primary way to punish Steel-types like Archaludon and Kingambit for super effective damage. Notably, the Speed drop acts as team support when Greninja is about to be KOed, as lowering a foe's Speed allows a teammate to come in and finish off a threat that might otherwise outspeed the rest of the team.

  • Water Shuriken: For teams that lack a priority option, Water Shuriken allows Greninja to act as a revenge killer after the Focus Sash is consumed, enabling it to pick off opposing Focus Sash users like Sneasler and Meowscarada or clean up weakened foes like Mega Gengar that would otherwise outspeed and KO it.

  • Toxic Spikes: Toxic Spikes provides good utility against bulkier teams and allows Greninja to wear down defensive foes like Umbreon and Primarina that it cannot break through directly, providing support for the rest of the team to clean up later.

  • Modest versus Timid: With a Modest nature, Greninja remains faster than threats such as Garchomp, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Kangaskhan. A Timid nature is an alternative option if moving first against faster Pokemon like Meowscarada, Mega Lucario, and Sneasler is more important than the extra power.

All-out Attacker.description:
• Greninja uses its excellent Speed, Protean-boosted coverage, and either Greninjite or Choice Scarf to revenge kill offensive threats and pressure teams with its endless range of coverage.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam is one of Greninja's most important attacks, dealing heavy damage to Dragon- and Ground-types such as Garchomp, Dragonite, and Hydreigon.

  • Sludge Wave: Sludge Wave lets Greninja pressure Fairy- and Grass-types such as Mega Floette, Primarina, Sylveon, Mega Clefable, and Mega Meganium.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse gives Greninja a reliable attack against Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Mega Gengar, Aegislash, Mega Delphox, and Ceruledge.

  • Hydro Pump versus Surf: Hydro Pump is preferred on Greninjite sets for its higher damage output, notably giving Greninja a stronger attack against Hippowdon. Surf is weaker but more accurate, making it more reliable when Greninja needs to revenge kill without risking a miss.

  • Low Kick versus Grass Knot versus U-turn: Low Kick lets Greninja punish heavier Dark- and Steel-types such as Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Archaludon while also chipping Snorlax, Mega Kangaskhan, and Mega Lucario hard. Meanwhile, Grass Knot is Greninja's strongest option against Hippowdon and Basculegion-M while also hitting Mega Blastoise hard. U-turn is especially useful on Choice Scarf sets, letting Greninja pivot out of unfavorable matchups and keep momentum against switch-ins like Umbreon, Mega Scizor, and Gyarados.

  • Mega Evolving Greninja: Greninjite sets do not always need to Mega Evolve immediately, as staying in base forme gives Greninja one extra Protean type change before Mega Evolving. This can help Greninja play around foes' attacks or boost the power of a specific coverage move, but delaying Mega Evolution also means giving up Mega Greninja's improved stats for that turn.

Items

  • Greninjite versus Choice Scarf: Mega Greninja boasts the freedom to switch moves and better immediate attacking stats, making it harder for opponents to play around its coverage. Choice Scarf's extra Speed gives Greninja stronger revenge killing utility, letting it outspeed boosted threats that Mega Greninja cannot.

Other Options

  • Extrasensory: Extrasensory can be used to hit Mega Venusaur and the uncommon Toxapex, which otherwise handles many of Greninja's common coverage options.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide can be used on mixed sets to counter Mega Charizard Y, notably OHKOing maximum HP variants even with a negative Attack nature. However, fitting it means giving up one of Greninja's more useful coverage moves.

SP Spreads

  • 8 HP / 32 SpA / 26 Spe with Timid or Naive: This spread lets Mega Greninja outspeed Mega Lopunny while giving it a decent chance to survive Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp's Outrage. A Naive nature should be used on mixed sets to avoid weakening physical coverage moves such as Low Kick.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest or Rash: This spread maximizes Greninja's Speed and Special Attack investment, giving Mega Greninja's Hydro Pump and Grass Knot the power to OHKO specially defensive Hippowdon. A Rash nature should be used on mixed sets to avoid weakening physical coverage moves such as Rock Slide.

X: Life Giver (Bulky Setup).description:
• Mega Floette's deceptively decent bulk and access to Fairy Aura-boosted Draining Kiss make it an incredibly sturdy late-game sweeper on bulky offense teams, as it's able to quickly snowball into high damage and healing. However, its shallow movepool means that it typically needs opposing Pokemon that resist its Fairy-type STAB attacks to be weakened beforehand.

  • Calm Mind + Draining Kiss: The combination of Calm Mind and Draining Kiss gives Mega Floette amazing longevity, letting it set up on and subsequently defeat even special attackers that hit it super effectively like Archaludon.

  • Moonblast: Moonblast is more immediately threatening than Draining Kiss, giving Mega Floette a consistent damaging option in situations where it's unable to boost its Special Attack. Moonblast is also particularly useful for picking off Pokemon that have already been weakened by Draining Kiss but would not be KOed by the weaker move.

  • Light of Ruin: Light of Ruin is a nuclear option that provides similar offensive utility to Moonblast. Owing to its higher Base Power, it's a lot more potent for closing out games than Moonblast—for example, Light of Ruin can always OHKO Basculegion-M and has a good chance of doing the same to maximum HP Kingambit—though its recoil damage can make Mega Floette more prone to being revenge killed.

  • Synthesis: Synthesis provides consistent healing, granting more time for Mega Floette to boost its stats before Draining Kiss can threaten the opponent's Pokemon. Synthesis can also be used to stall out Mega Charizard Y's sun if needed, buying an opportunity for Mega Floette to set up.

Other Options

  • Psychic: Psychic has a niche use in giving Mega Floette a way to deal with defensive Poison-types—in particular Toxapex, which otherwise can shrug off its Fairy-type attacks and remove its stat boosts with Haze—though giving up the consistent offensive power of Moonblast or Light of Ruin can greatly limit its damage output in situations where it can't use Calm Mind.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 29 Def / 5 SpA with Modest: This spread aims to patch Mega Floette's lower physical bulk, ensuring Garchomp's Earthquake is a 3HKO, while the investment in Special Attack allows it to always OHKO even maximum HP sets in return with a +1 Draining Kiss.

Y: Life Taker (Offensive).description:
• With enough Speed to outpace common threats like Mega Dragonite and both of Charizard's Mega Evolutions, as well as Speed tying with Garchomp, Mega Floette can act as a powerful sweeper capable of doing immense damage with Fairy Aura-boosted Moonblast and Light of Ruin.

  • Moonblast versus Draining Kiss: Mega Floette greatly appreciates the additional damage provided by Moonblast, notably OHKOing offensive Archaludon and all Garchomp sets without needing to use Calm Mind, though Draining Kiss can still be useful to help Mega Floette avoid being worn down especially if you're choosing to forgo Synthesis.

  • Psychic: Psychic gives Mega Floette an option to hit Poison-types that would otherwise wall it, notably 2HKOing physically defensive Mega Venusaur and OHKOing Mega Gengar after Stealth Rock damage, though be aware that Mega Gengar has a good chance of OHKOing Mega Floette itself with Sludge Wave if it hasn't already buffed its Special Defense.

  • Substitute: Mega Floette can use Substitute to take advantage of passive Pokemon like Umbreon and Hippowdon that lack Whirlwind by blocking their status moves, letting it set up with Calm Mind. Substitute can also be useful to prevent being worn down by Fake Out cycling from the likes of Mega Lopunny and Sneasler.

Aegislash.comments:
Speed SP Benchmarks

  • 1 Speed: This Speed investment allows Aegislash to outspeed uninvested Primarina and Clefable.

  • 2 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Tyranitar.

  • 6 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Scizor and Umbreon.

  • 7 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Skeledirge.

  • 8 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Corviknight.

  • 16 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Mega Scizor.

  • 21 Speed: This allows it to outspeed uninvested Mega Meganium and Mega Venusaur.

Physical Attacker.description:
• With its incredible stats, boasting sets of some of the highest offensive and defensive stats of any non-Mega Evolved Pokemon in the format; access to a powerful STAB attack with little drawback in Poltergeist; and its amazing typing, Aegislash is a potent physical wallbreaker that few Pokemon can switch in on without taking serious damage. Shadow Sneak also gives it the option to act as a revenge killer, allowing it to clean up weakened teams and remain useful late-game.

  • Swords Dance: With a Swords Dance boost, Aegislash is able to tear through even defensive teams, and thanks to Shield forme's stellar defenses, it can often find opportunities to set up, especially against common Pokemon like Corviknight, Archaludon, Mega Floette, and Sneasler. At +2, Poltergeist OHKOes bulky Primarina and Rotom-W sets, and Shadow Sneak OHKOes the likes of Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar.

  • King's Shield: At the cost of some offensive power, King's Shield provides Aegislash with much greater longevity, particularly when combined with Leftovers. By using King's Shield to first lower their Attack, Aegislash can take hits from and subsequently OHKO physically attacking counters that commonly run all-out attacking sets like Mega Lopunny and Meowscarada, making it much more difficult for offensive teams to reliably deal with.

  • Close Combat versus Sacred Sword: Aegislash appreciates Fighting-type coverage, which lets it hit Dark- and Normal-type Pokemon for super effective damage. Sets lacking King's Shield typically prefer the additional damage that Close Combat provides, which gives Aegislash the ability to always OHKO Mega Lucario as well as Mega Lopunny and Hydreigon on the switch in. Such sets don't care about Close Combat's drawback thanks to Blade forme's already low defensive stats. With this said, Swords Dance sets can still benefit from Sacred Sword ignoring stat boosts, which prevents Iron Defense Corviknight from using Aegislash to set up.

Other Options

  • Brave Nature: King's Shield variants of Aegislash can run a Brave nature, allowing them to always be slower than neutral-nature Primarina and therefore always be in the more defensive Shield forme when taking damage from its attacks. This comes at the cost of a worse matchup against opposing Adamant Aegislash, however, as the one-on-one is often decided by which Pokemon hits Poltergeist first.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head provides a STAB attack that, unlike Poltergeist, doesn't rely on the opposing Pokemon holding an item. This allows Aegislash to deal consistent damage throughout the game if it's paired with a Knock Off user like Meowscarada, as well as against common Sitrus Berry users like Hippowdon. Iron Head's lower Base Power can hinder Aegislash's ability to sweep, however.

Items

  • Spell Tag: Spell Tag makes Aegislash's Ghost-type STAB attacks even more potent, making Poltergeist a guaranteed OHKO on Primarina after Stealth Rock damage and giving it a chance to OHKO physically defensive Corviknight after a Swords Dance.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is generally preferred on King's Shield variants, which greatly appreciate passively healing while they protect themselves. However, Leftovers can still be useful on Swords Dance sets thanks to the pressure Aegislash's massive damage output puts on the opponent to make defensive switches, which often buys it free turns to heal.

  • Focus Sash: Swords Dance sets can make use of Focus Sash to set up on would-be threats like Mega Gengar and threaten a sweep against frail teams with a boosted Shadow Sneak.

Mixed Attacker.description:
• Aegislash is a popular threat in BSS thanks to its good defensive typing and priority. This set trades damage for coverage and better offensive versatility against physical walls.

  • Shadow Ball: With Shadow Ball and Special Attack investment, Aegislash fares better against Corviknight and Archaludon due to their low Special Defense. Since Corviknight is prone to using U-turn, Aegislash's Quiet nature allows it to hit the incoming Pokemon instead. Aegislash also heavily threatens Iron Defense Mega Metagross by running Shadow Ball instead of Poltergeist.

  • Shadow Sneak: Aegislash's high offensive stats in Blade Forme mean that Shadow Sneak still has wide utility for revenge killing or dealing damage to faster foes like Basculegion-M, Mega Delphox, Mega Gengar, and Focus Sash Greninja.

  • King's Shield: King's Shield is useful against physical attackers like Meowscarada, Mega Lopunny, and Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott. Lowering a foe's Attack allows Aegislash to win many one-on-one scenarios it otherwise wouldn't. However, Contrary users like Mega Staraptor can gain an Attack boost from King's Shield when using Blaze Kick.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat still deals heavy damage to Mega Lucario, Mega Lopunny, Mega Greninja, and Meowscarada. The lack of full Attack investment does mean that Aegislash won't consistently OHKO the first two without chip damage, so having an entry hazard setter is generally recommended with this set.

Other Options

  • Flash Cannon versus Iron Head: Flash Cannon provides an additional STAB option against Fairy-types like Alolan Ninetales and makes use of Aegislash's investment in Special Attack. It does well against Mega Floette, though Iron Head deals more damage even without Attack investment and has a chance to KO offensive variants. Flash Cannon also deals the most damage against Mega Scrafty and Mega Staraptor.

  • Sacred Sword: Sacred Sword does well against Archaludon and provides coverage without the cost of lowering Aegislash's defensive stats.

Items

  • Spell Tag: Spell Tag provides a blanket boost to Ghost-type attacks, allowing Shadow Ball to consistently 2HKO uninvested Archaludon and Corviknight and OHKO Mega Metagross.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers has good synergy with King's Shield, allowing Aegislash to recover out of KO range while protecting itself. King's Shield lowering the Attack of foes that use contact moves can also give Aegislash more opportunities to recover with Leftovers.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb provides a helpful damage boost against Pokemon that Aegislash cannot quite OHKO with coverage. Examples include Hisuian Samurott, Mega Lucario, and Mega Lopunny with Close Combat, as well as Mega Floette with Flash Cannon. However, this cuts heavily into Aegislash's longevity.

Primarina.comments:
Special Defense SP Benchmarks

  • 32 HP and 15 Special Defense: With Sitrus Berry, this allows Primarina to avoid the 2HKO from Modest Mega Dragonite's Thunderbolt.

  • 32 HP and 17 Special Defense: This allows Primarina to avoid the OHKO from Timid Mega Gengar's Sludge Wave.

Speed SP Benchmarks

  • 6 Speed: This lets Primarina outspeed uninvested Scizor and Umbreon.

  • 7 Speed: This lets it outspeed uninvested Skeledirge.

  • 8 Speed: This lets it outspeed uninvested Corviknight.

  • 16 Speed: This lets it outspeed uninvested Mega Scizor.

Offensive Utility.description:
• With excellent natural bulk and a stellar typing combination, Primarina is a premier balance attacker that can provide both excellent offensive trading and strong support options.

  • Aqua Jet: While somewhat weak on Primarina, Aqua Jet is still an excellent move for picking off weakened foes and finishing off Focus Sash users like Garchomp.

  • Flip Turn versus Encore: Flip Turn lets Primarina function as a bulky pivot against faster threats, while Encore lets Primarina disrupt slower, bulkier threats like Hippowdon.

  • Modest versus Quiet: Even if it does weaken Aqua Jet, Modest is the no-nonsense option especially if Primarina is running Encore. On the other hand, Quiet can be run to preserve Aqua Jet's power while also making Primarina a slower pivot with Flip Turn.

Other Options

  • Ice Beam: Despite Moonblast already hitting Dragon-types very hard, Ice Beam can be used to catch bulkier Garchomp sets that survive Moonblast by surprise. It’s also a good tool to pressure Mega Meganium on a predicted switch, as Modest Primarina's Ice Beam can 2HKO maximum HP builds.

  • Psychic Noise: Psychic Noise is Primarina's only hope of taking on Mega Venusaur, dealing respectable damage and temporarily stopping any Synthesis or Leech Seed healing.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is the most reliable source of recovery for attacking sets.

  • Mystic Water: Mystic Water is an alternative to healing items that synergizes better with Torrent, allowing Primarina's Sparkling Aria to hit extra hard once it's at low health.

  • Leftovers: If Sitrus Berry is needed elsewhere on the team, Leftovers is a decent alternative for healing.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash can be used with fully offensive spreads, allowing Primarina to activate Torrent more easily against targets such as Mega Gengar.

Other SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 2 SpA / 32 SpD with Calm or Sassy: With this spread, Primarina can lean harder into being a special cushion for its team. In particular, it almost always avoids the 2HKO from Modest Mega Dragonite's Thunderbolt.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest: A fully offensive spread should always be used for Focus Sash sets. It also greatly increases Primarina's ability to disrupt with Encore.

Mimikyu.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Swords Dance.description:
• Disguise's incredible power in a format where Item Clause is in effect makes Mimikyu an excellent sweeper and revenge killer despite its mediocre stats!

  • Shadow Sneak: Despite its paltry power, Shadow Sneak is perfect for picking off weakened threats like Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox.

  • Shadow Claw: When Disguise is still intact, Shadow Claw paired with Life Orb or Spell Tag lets Mimikyu OHKO offensive Mega Metagross, offensive Mega Gengar, and Mega Delphox.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb's power boost makes it by far Mimikyu's best item, beefing up its mediocre Attack stat enough to KO key threats after a boost, such as offensive Primarina and Mega Blaziken.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Mimikyu prefers to juice up its Attack stat with Adamant to pick off as many threats as possible with Shadow Sneak, but Jolly is still worth considering for outspeeding opposing Mimikyu and Modest Mega Dragonite.

Other Options

  • Curse: Curse is effective at punishing foes that may attempt to set up on Mimikyu like Mega Scizor, Iron Defense Mega Metagross, and Iron Defense Corviknight. Sacrificing Mimikyu with Curse when its weakened can also be an effective way to bring in dangerous sweepers like Garchomp and Mega Delphox. Finally, Curse lets Mimikyu put your opponent's last remaining Pokemon on a timer, potentially clinching you a win if Mimikyu doesn't have enough power to KO them.

  • Wood Hammer: Wood Hammer crushes even the most defensive Hippowdon after a boost when using an Adamant nature and Life Orb, a threat Mimikyu usually has little business breaking through early on. It also allows Mimikyu to revenge kill offensive Primarina.

  • Drain Punch: Drain Punch's healing isn't particularly helpful for such an offensive Mimikyu set, but it's the only way to OHKO Kingambit after a boost.

Other Items

  • Mimikyu should almost always use Life Orb, but other options can be considered if another teammate needs it.

  • Spell Tag: Spell Tag is Mimikyu's second best offensive item, turning Shadow Claw into an effective revenge killing option with an Adamant nature against Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox, as well as retaining the key OHKO after a boost against offensive Mega Metagross.

  • Scope Lens: Scope Lens gives Shadow Claw a 50% chance to land a critical hit, meaning boosted Mimikyu can potentially ruin Iron Defense Mega Metagross attempting to stonewall a sweep.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry is a great response against status inducers, with Yawn Umbreon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash being particularly big targets for Mimikyu to surprise.

Swiss Army Knife (Trick Room Support).description:
• Mimikyu offers role compression with its Disguise ability to stop foes from sweeping, Shadow Sneak to pick up KOs, disrupting resilient foes with Curse, and speed control as a Trick Room setter!

  • Trick Room: Trick Room provides speed control for very slow Pokemon like Mega Mawile, Aegislash, and Kingambit. Variants of naturally fast Pokemon like Garchomp and Meowscarada that do not fully invest in Speed or use a Choice Scarf also appreciate Trick Room, as it lets them move before faster variants of themselves. With Disguise, Mimikyu can absorb a hit from an opposing Trick Room sweeper and use Trick Room to restore the normal Speed order, thus allowing its team to countersweep!

  • Curse: At low HP, Curse grants a clean exit for Mimikyu and lets it safely bring in another teammate. It can also put opposing defensive Pokemon and Baton Pass chains or recipients on a timer.

  • Shadow Sneak: Shadow Sneak lets Mimikyu pick up KOs against faster or problematic foes that can threaten Mimikyu's partners. With Life Orb, Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak always 2HKOes Basculegion-M, Mega Starmie, and Mega Gengar.

  • Play Rough: With Life Orb, Mimikyu's Play Rough has a good chance to OHKO Mega Gyarados and usually OHKOes uninvested Garchomp.

Items

  • Life Orb: Life Orb's boost improves or guarantees the odds of achieving the aforementioned OHKOs and 2HKOs, which would otherwise be harder to achieve with type-enhancing items. If Mimikyu is in range of fainting from Life Orb recoil, it can attack the foe, faint, and make way for another teammate, which can come in clutch if Taunt prevents Mimikyu from using Curse!

  • Mental Herb: Mental Herb gives Mimikyu a second chance to set Trick Room or use Curse if Taunted. For team modes that rely on Trick Room sweepers as a win condition, this can be a more consistent option.

SP Spreads

These SP spreads minimize Stealth Rock damage and let Mimikyu use Curse twice without fainting. With Disguise, it can also survive a five-hit Icicle Spear from Adamant Mamoswine; if Disguise is broken, Mimikyu can still take Triple Axel from Adamant Protean Meowscarada. As Disguise is ignored by Mold Breaker, Mimikyu will always survive Waterfall or Crunch from Jolly Mega Gyarados at full HP after a Dragon Dance.

  • 29 HP / 30 Atk / 7 Def with Adamant: This spread can be used with Life Orb. The additional investment in Defense improves Mimikyu's survivability alongside Life Orb recoil, giving it a small chance to survive Bullet Punch from Adamant Mega Metagross after its Disguise is broken.

  • 29 HP / 32 Atk / 5 Def with Adamant: This spread can be used with Mental Herb. If Disguise is broken, Mimikyu has a good chance to survive Bullet Punch from Adamant Mega Metagross.

Corviknight.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Physically Defensive.description:
• Corviknight serves as an excellent physical wall, with its incredible typing enabling it to handle physical attackers and Ground-types such as Tyranitar, Garchomp, and Hippowdon with ease.

  • Body Press: Body Press is the main offensive option, weaponizing Corviknight's good natural bulk to dispose of threats such as Meowscarada, Excadrill, and Umbreon safely.

  • Iron Head: If a secondary offensive option is needed, Iron Head allows Corviknight to actually threaten Mimikyu and Sylveon along with Primarina and Mega Floette in a pinch.

  • Iron Defense: Iron Defense improves Corviknight's Defense and Body Press's damage, enabling it to shrug off physical attackers like Dragonite and Sneasler completely.

  • Taunt: Taunt allows Corviknight to shut down Umbreon and Hippowdon, preventing them from forcing Corviknight out with tools such as Yawn, and prevents multiple turns of setup from the likes of Dragon Dance Dragonite.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers allows Corviknight to safely stay on the field for multiple turns while it accrues Iron Defense boosts.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can provide a solid quick burst of healing, enabling Corviknight to have HP to spare while combating foes such as Tyranitar and Mega Gyarados.

Abilities

  • Pressure: Pressure punishes Pokemon reliant on low-PP moves like Garchomp, which needs Stone Edge to reliably damage Corviknight, by quickly draining their moves' PP; Pressure also helps Corviknight handle opposing Corviknight by letting it outlast their Body Press's PP.

  • Mirror Armor: Mirror Armor punishes Intimidate from Gyarados, forcing it to set up with Dragon Dance longer, along with Special Defense drops from the likes of Espathra's Lumina Crash and Gengar's Shadow Ball, which can help force them out as Corviknight pivots to a special attacker.

Specially Defensive.description:
• With a specially defensive SP spread, Corviknight can still maintain its role of checking Ground-types like Hippowdon as with the a physically defensive spread while also expanding its reaches and allowing it to directly take on special attackers such as Mega Meganium and Gengar.

  • Body Press and Iron Defense: Body Press and Iron Defense can allow Corviknight to still check more physically leaning threats such as Mega Lopunny once it gets going while also making it capable of directly combating Archaludon that lack Electro Shot.

  • Brave Bird: Brave Bird is an alternative offensive tool for Corviknight to bust up Mega Venusaur and Primarina.

  • Taunt: Taunt shuts down Hippowdon and Sylveon's attempts to force it out with Yawn and prevents Corviknight from being safely set up on by the likes of Hydreigon.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers can soften the blow of the recoil from Brave Bird.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst healing helps Corviknight take on Mega Meganium and quickly recover from an untimely bit of Brave Bird recoil.

Abilities

  • Pressure: Pressure helps Corviknight handle Primarina by depleting its Sparkling Aria PP more quickly as well as allowing it to quickly expend Garchomp's Stone Edge PP.

  • Mirror Armor: Mirror Armor annoys Gyarados by turning Intimidate against it, along with bouncing Special Defense drops back against the likes of Lumina Crash Espathra and Shadow Ball Gengar as Corviknight pivots to a special attacker.

Dual Screens.description:
• Thanks to Prankster, Grimmsnarl is a consistent dual screens setter that can enable sweepers like Mega Gyarados, Nasty Plot Mega Delphox, and Swords Dance Garchomp to safely set up. Though it lacks the Speed and offensive presence of Aurora Veil setter Alolan Ninetales, Grimmsnarl's defensive typing and access to useful disruption moves help it find a place on bulkier teams.

  • Spirit Break: Spirit Break has greater accuracy than Play Rough, with both moves 2HKOing offensive Garchomp and Mega Gyarados, and its secondary effect can punish specially offensive checks like Primarina and Archaludon that want to switch in on Grimmsnarl.

  • Parting Shot: Prankster gives Parting Shot increased priority, allowing the otherwise slow Grimmsnarl to build momentum on top of providing it with another way to reduce the damage dealt by the opposing Pokemon. However, Parting Shot will fail if used against a Pokemon with Good as Gold or Clear Body, preventing Grimmsnarl from switching, so it should be used with caution if the opponent can switch in a Gholdengo or a non-Mega-Evolved Metagross.

  • Taunt: Taunt shuts down supportive Pokemon like Hippowdon and defensive Garchomp, letting Grimmsnarl act as an effective counter lead. It can also prevent Pokemon like Volcarona and Mega Blaziken from taking advantage of Grimmsnarl's passivity by setting up on it.

  • Foul Play: Foul Play provides an alternative attack that can punish setup and is particularly effective against Mega Metagross and Aegislash. However, opting to stay in against these Pokemon will often result in Grimmsnarl taking significant damage, which can compromise its ability to set up dual screens late-game.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpD with Impish: Running a physically defensive SP spread allows Grimmsnarl to always survive a Bullet Punch followed by a second Bullet Punch behind Reflect from Adamant Mega Metagross and Mega Lucario, brings Adamant Life Orb Mimikyu's Play Rough to a 3HKO behind Reflect, and helps it act as a late-game check to Basculegion-M.

  • 32 HP / 18 Def / 16 SpD with Careful: Running some Special Defense brings Timid Glimmora's Sludge Wave and Modest Archaludon's Flash Cannon to a 3HKO behind Light Screen and gives Grimmsnarl a very good chance to avoid the 2HKO from Modest Primarina's Moonblast under the same conditions. Investing the rest of its Stat Points in Defense allows Grimmsnarl to always survive Adamant Mega Scizor's Bullet Punch.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Basculgion-M is enjoying a fantastic offensive type combination in the current metagame, which, when combined with Adaptability, makes it a standout pick as a late-game sweeper with Last Respects and a potent early-game scout with Flip Turn.

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf gives Basculegion-M the Speed it needs to chunk foes and get out safely early-game while also allowing you to bring it in late-game without spending a turn to set up Agility. However, Basculegion-M's pitiful base 78 Speed means that it will be outsped by most of the other Choice Scarf users in the format, as well as most Dragon Dance users, so you need to be careful when positioning Basculegion-M.

  • Wave Crash: Wave Crash will be Basculegion-M's primary early-game damage option if you elect to not pivot it out.

  • Last Respects: Even after just one team member is KOed, Last Respects becomes an extremely potent move that's very difficult to switch into, and it gives Basculegion-M immense sweeping power once both allies have fainted.

  • Flip Turn: Adaptability allows Flip Turn to deal notable damage for a pivoting move.

  • Aqua Jet: Adaptability-boosted Aqua Jet does a considerable amount of damage and can get Basculegion-M out of trouble against other priority users or Speed-boosted foes.

Other Options

  • Ice Fang: Ice Fang provides coverage against Dragon-types and threatens Garchomp and Dragonite right out of the gate.

  • Head Smash: Head Smash gives Basculegion-M a heavily damaging coverage option that threatens Gyarados and Dragonite.

Offensive.description:
• This Agility set gives Basculegion-M the freedom to outspeed and threaten the majority of its metagame-relevant foes while enabling it to use multiple moves.

  • Opposing Priority Users: While setting up Agility can make Basculegion-M an absolutely terrifying sweeper, late-game checks such as Aegislash, Mimikyu, and Kingambit are quite popular in the current metagame, so be careful when you see these during Team Preview.

  • Adamant Nature: Agility's boost is going to give Basculegion-M plenty of Speed to set up its sweep. As Basculegion-M lacks an Attack-boosting setup move, an Adamant nature is preferred over Jolly. Adamant Basculegion-M is already outspeeding Choice Scarf Garchomp with an Agility boost, while a Jolly nature won't allow it to outspeed the likes of Choice Scarf Jolly Meowscarada.

Items

  • Mystic Water versus Spell Tag: These items will allow Basculegion-M's STAB moves to do hilariously high damage. Mystic Water allows Basculegion-M to OHKO physically defensive Hippowdon with Wave Crash and has the added bonus of juicing up Aqua Jet's damage when it needs to rely on priority. On the other hand, Spell Tag will allow Last Respects to tear through walls, letting it OHKO maximum HP Mega Scizor after Stealth Rock at 150 Base Power.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash ensures that Basculegion-M is going to tank a hit while it sets up Agility, but because entry hazards are very popular in the current metagame, saving your Focus Sash user for last can be a risky venture.

Sneasler.overview: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

Unburden Sweeper.description:
• With the powerful Unburden ability, Sneasler can become a dangerous cleaner that wrecks havoc on frailer teams.

  • Throat Chop versus Shadow Claw : When covering Psychic- and Ghost-types, Throat Chop is usually preferred for its higher power over Shadow Claw. However, Adamant Sneasler with Shadow Claw has about a 50/50 chance to knock out offensive Mimikyu after Disguise breaks.

  • Swords Dance : If allowed to set up a Swords Dance, Sneasler can quickly spiral out of control and even overpower Hippowdon and Corviknight if they have been chipped.

  • Fake Out: Fake Out can help get targets into KO range of its more powerful attacks, and the priority helps Sneasler catch faster foes prior to activating Unburden.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is usually preferred to maximize sweeping potential, and with Unburden active, Sneasler can effortlessly outrun even Choice Scarf Dragapult. WIth maximum investment, Adamant Sneasler also maintains enough Speed to outrun threats like Mega Glimmora and unboosted Garchomp before Unburden's boost. Jolly gives Sneasler a little more consistency, allowing it to outrun more threats such as Mega Starmie and Focus Sash Gengar before Unburden activates.

Other Options

  • Acrobatics: Acrobatics is Sneasler's best move against threats like Mega Venusaur, Volcarona, and opposing Sneasler, though the move's damage is reliant on Sneasler consuming its item beforehand.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide landing a clean OHKO on Mega Charizard Y is huge, but its uses are otherwise limited.

  • Fling: Fling with King's Rock or Light Ball is the most flexible method of triggering Sneasler's Unburden, but the sacrifice to damage and coverage makes it a hard sell.

Items

  • White Herb: White Herb synergizes fantastically with Sneasler, allowing it to activate Unburden through its best attack Close Combat while also nullifying the defense drops once. White Herb can also function as insurance against Intimidate users.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can give the somewhat frail Sneasler a bit more survivability, especially against priority attacks. However, it does make Sneasler reliant on the opponent to trigger Unburden for it.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry puts Sneasler into a more niche role for its team, focused on countering status users like Yawn Umbreon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash.

Meowscarada.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Meowscarada's ability Protean and good base Speed combined with Choice Scarf make it an extremely versatile solution to many speedy threats such as Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, Mega Gyarados after a Dragon Dance, and Mega Lopunny.

  • Flower Trick: Because it always lands a critical hit, Meowscarada's signature move is a very consistent source of damage against Intimidate Gyarados and Shell Smash Blastoise behind dual screens. It notably 2HKOes Hippowdon and Garchomp and OHKOes Basculegion-M and Primarina.

  • Triple Axel: Triple Axel covers targets that resist Grass- and Dark-type moves, OHKOing foes such as Multiscale Dragonite, Focus Sash Garchomp, Starapator, and Hydreigon. Triple Axel can also 2HKO both Mega Charizard X and Mega Charizard Y, making it very difficult for them to switch in and forcing Mega Charizard X to refrain from using Dragon Dance, as it still won't outspeed Meowscarada after one boost.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off allows Meowscarada to remove Leftovers and do decent damage to Aegislash. It can be used to remove Leftovers and Sitrus Berry from Archaludon and Leftovers from Corviknight as they switch in. It will also 2HKO Mega Evolutions such as Mega Delphox, Mega Starmie, and Mega Gengar.

  • Thunder Punch: Thunder Punch is useful against Mega Charizard Y, providing more consistent damage compared to Triple Axel. It can also be used to finish off a weakened Corviknight.

  • U-turn: U-turn maintains momentum against Meowscarada's checks and hard counters, such as Blaziken, Kingambit, Corviknight, Mega Scizor, Archaludon, and Mega Venusaur. It will also OHKO opposing Choice Scarf Meowscarada, leading to a coin flip for momentum.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature provides some niche benefits, as it is what allows Meowscarada to outspeed Timid Choice Scarf Greninja, but the main reason is to compete with opposing Meowscarada. As Meowscarada's Speed is already high with Choice Scarf, an Adamant nature allows it to more consistently OHKO Mega Gyarados with Flower Trick as well as Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar with Knock Off.

Other Options

  • Throat Chop: Throat Chop can be used as a substitute for Knock Off. It does more consistent damage against Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox, since Mega Stones can't be removed. It also stops Skeledirge from using Torch Song.

  • Low Kick: Low Kick can be useful against Archaludon and Kingambit.

Focus Sash.description:
• Focus Sash Meowscarada is useful thanks to its ability to 2HKO many foes and strike first with Sucker Punch. Focus Sash Meowscarada can take on Pokemon such as Glimmora, Mega Delphox, Mega Gyarados, Mega Greninja, and Mega Gengar one-on-one.

  • Flower Trick: Flower Trick is very helpful against Water- and Ground-type Pokemon, providing consistent damage against Gyarados, Primarina, and Hippowdon.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch gives Meowscarada an edge in finishing off faster Pokemon such as Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar. It also provides good damage against Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, and a strong chance to 2HKO offensive Mega Metagross

  • Triple Axel versus Knock Off: Triple Axel is great for beating Garchomp and Multiscale Dragonite, as well as hitting neutral targets such as Sneasler and both of Charizard's Mega Evolutions. Knock Off is a strong Dark-type move that doesn't count on Meowscarada's foe attacking first while also removing an item. It is particularly helpful against Ceruledge and Aegislash, as they will not always attack when Meowscarada uses Sucker Punch.

  • U-turn: U-turn maintains momentum against Meowscarada's hard counters, such as Archaludon or Corviknight.

  • Taunt: Taunt can avoid messy situations where your opponent's Pokemon tries to set up on Meowscarada, letting it stop Hippowdon and Mega Scizor from using Stealth Rock and Swords Dance, respectively.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature is heavily preferred for outspeeding Jolly Mega Metagross, a threat Meowscarada has the potential to surprise one-on-one.

Other Options

  • Toxic Spikes: Toxic Spikes can be strong in longer drawn-out games. This does little to alleviate Meowscarada's poor matchup against Steel-types, though.

  • Overgrow: Overgrow has good synergy with Focus Sash for boosting Flower Trick.

  • Low Kick: Low Kick is an option against Archaludon and Kingambit.

Physical Wall.description:
• Skeledirge's decent bulk and access to Unaware allow it to act as a check to some of the most threatening physical sweepers in the metagame, notably walling Mega Blaziken, Scizor, as well as IronPress variants of Mega Metagross and Corviknight. Its strong offensive typing and potential to snowball with Torch Song additionally keep it from being too passive to fit on offensive teams, setting it apart from other physical walls.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Burning physical attackers makes it even easier for Skeledirge to tank their attacks, allowing it to take on Pokemon like Mimikyu and Jolly Garchomp that can otherwise deal significant damage to it. The threat of Will-O-Wisp also makes it difficult for the opponent to safely switch in physical attackers that Skeledirge fears, like Mega Gyarados.

  • Yawn: Though Yawn lacks the potential to flip matchups that Will-O-Wisp has, it can be effective for buying free turns for Skeledirge to use Torch Song or Slack Off. Forcing switches with Yawn can also be useful to rack up entry hazard damage over the course of a game if Skeledirge is paired with an entry hazard setter.

  • Shadow Ball versus Hex: Shadow Ball lets Skeledirge deal consistent damage to Pokemon that it doesn't want to waste a turn inflicting status on and is especially useful against burn-immune Pokemon like Mega Delphox. Though more reliant on prediction, Hex pairs well with Will-O-Wisp against bulkier teams, and its greater power can help Skeledirge deal significant damage to Pokemon it typically struggles with, like Toxapex and Primarina, on the switch-in.

Other Options

  • Encore: After switching in, Skeledirge can potentially use Encore to lock slower Pokemon it struggles with into using ineffective moves, for example forcing Primarina to repeat Moonblast or Calm Mind, or Aegislash to repeat Swords Dance. This is, however, much less effective against faster Pokemon that typically won't give Skeledirge an opportunity to use Encore.

Items

  • Leftovers versus Sitrus Berry: Leftovers greatly increases Skeledirge's longevity, making it less reliant on Slack Off to stay healthy, and it can often find free turns to heal thanks to the switches it forces. Though Sitrus Berry's burst healing is less conducive to keeping a wall like Skeledirge healthy in the long run, it can make Skeledirge more consistent in certain matchups; for example, it allows Skeledirge to always avoid the 2HKO from Adamant Life Orb Mimikyu's Shadow Claw.

  • Kasib Berry: Kasib Berry allows Skeledirge to be more aggressive against Mimikyu, as it does not have to risk missing Will-O-Wisp to beat it, and provides utility by causing Poltergeist to fail once consumed, allowing Skeledirge to wall Ceruledge and physical Aegislash. If needed, Kasib Berry can also let Skeledirge stay in against special-attacking Ghost-types that could otherwise OHKO it, like Mega Gengar and Gholdengo, as well as opposing Skeledirge, and deal significant damage to them with its STAB attacks.

  • No Item: Running no item on Skeledirge causes Poltergeist to always fail against it, giving Skeledirge the same utility in this regard as Kasib Berry, and weakens Knock Off from the likes of Meowscarada and Scizor, at the cost of passive healing.

Focus Sash.description:
• Ceruledge's strong typing and access to Swords Dance make it a powerful offensive presence, which includes the ability to overwhelm targets like Corviknight and Volcarona that normally wall physical attackers well.

  • Weak Armor: The combination of Weak Armor and Focus Sash can turn Ceruledge into a deadly fast sweeper, making it risky for prominent physical threats like Mega Lopunny and Sneasler to attack it.

  • Shadow Sneak: Paired with Weak Armor, Ceruledge with Shadow Sneak can win priority wars it would otherwise lose, on top of being a strong cleaning attack in general.

  • Poltergeist: Poltergeist is Ceruledge's strongest STAB attack and best overall source of damage, but be careful against targets that potentially use Sitrus Berry or other consumable items; some checks like Toxapex will go without an item to render Poltergeist useless from the start!

  • Bitter Blade: Bitter Blade's strong recovery is useful after being taken down to its Focus Sash, potentially giving Ceruledge more of a buffer against priority moves. Against weaker attacks, it can also heal Ceruledge back to full so that it can still utilize Focus Sash.

  • Close Combat: After a Swords Dance, Close Combat has a high chance of OHKOing physically defensive versions of both Archaludon and Umbreon! It's also strong against Mega Gyarados, which will often Mega Evolve to resist Poltergeist and Shadow Sneak.

  • Beware of Garchomp: Be wary of Rough Skin Garchomp that try to switch into Ceruledge's Bitter Blade or Shadow Sneak, as the passive damage nullifies Focus Sash and leaves Ceruledge vulnerable. Scale Shot can also be problematic, since it can trigger Weak Armor's Defense drop several times, though usually four hits are required to OHKO.

Other Options

  • Jolly Nature: The loss in power can be problematic elsewhere, but going Jolly over Adamant with the given SP spread will allow Ceruledge to outrun Choice Scarf Meowscarada after a single Weak Armor activation.

  • Flash Fire: Flash Fire allows Ceruledge to create momentum from the back by switching in on Mega Charizard Y's Fire-type attacks. Furthermore, an undamaged Ceruledge can take Stealth Rock chip damage and still always survive Timid Mega Charizard Y's Scorching Sands.

Special Wall.description:
• With impressive special bulk, Bellibolt can soak up most of the special attacks in the format and turn them into fuel to boost its own damage and even heal itself!

  • Volt Switch: Volt Switch is Bellibolt's means of pivoting out of incoming Electric-resistant foes. Positioning is important, as all of Bellibolt's offensive options are Electric-type. In a pinch, it can be used to inflict the extra damage needed to secure a KO in the event Parabolic Charge lacks the power needed.

  • Parabolic Charge: When boosted by Electromorphosis, Parabolic Charge becomes Bellibolt's primary offensive option. Its amazing HP-draining effect drastically increases Bellibolt's survivability while it deals solid damage.

  • Soak: Soak is a powerful utility option that makes foes weak to Bellibolt's attacks and usually removes their STAB boost from their attacks. It can also be used preemptively against incoming Ground-types, making them much more manageable to deal with.

  • Slack Off: Slack Off grants Bellibolt reliable healing and increased longevity in the event Parabolic Charge isn't a wise move.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry allows in-a-pinch healing, which can be very useful for taking on powerful attackers with high-Base Power moves, such as Draco Meteor Mega Dragonite.

  • Magnet: Magnet boosts the power of Bellibolt's attacks and, in the case of Parabolic Charge, its healing.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is a great option for Bellibolt if you're intending to make it take on more defensive teams, as when paired with Parabolic Charge, the consistent healing makes Bellibolt exceptionally difficult to damage with the lower offensive power of defensive teams.

SP Spread

  • 29 HP / 4 Def / 2 SpA / 28 SpD / 3 Spe with Calm: 29 HP and 4 Defense SPs guarantee Bellibolt will survive Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake. 3 Speed SPs allow it to outspeed uninvested Hippowdon and use Soak to enable pivoting. 2 Special Attack SPs ensure the OHKO on uninvested Garchomp with Parabolic Charge after Soak and Electromorphosis. The rest is placed into Special Defense to maximize bulk.

Other Options

  • Toxic: Toxic allows Bellibolt to stack on an extra layer of offensive pressure during sustained battles. It can also punish incoming Ground-types by placing them on a timer.

  • Acid Spray: Acid Spray improves Bellibolt's matchup against more defensive teams and Calm Mind users that attempt to take advantage of Bellibolt's semi-passive toolkit.

Kingambit.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.
Kingambit.comments:
Speed SP Benchmarks

  • Moving first means Kingambit can improve certain matchups like Primarina. Generally speaking, it is recommended to sacrifice bulk instead of offensive power if wanting to reallocate to Speed.

  • 3 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed negative Speed nature Aegislash.

  • 11 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested base 60 Speed targets such as Clefable before Mega Evolution, Primarina, and Aegislash.

  • 12 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Tyranitar.

  • 16 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Scizor before Mega Evolution.

  • 18 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Corviknight, though its superior bulk and access to Body Press mean that it is still overwhelmingly favored in the matchup.

  • 21 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Clefable, though keep in mind that Mega Clefable often receives Speed boosts from Baton Pass Espathra.

  • 26 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Scizor.

Swords Dance.description:
• With excellent typing, Supreme Overlord, and Sucker Punch, Kingambit is a powerful revenge killer and bulky attacker.

  • Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave: Sucker Punch helps pick off weakened attackers and is excellent insurance against late-game Choice Scarf users like Basculegion-M and Garchomp. Kowtow Cleave is usually needed as a second Dark-type attack, though, particularly for Substitute users like Mega Gengar that can play around Sucker Punch.

  • Swords Dance: Kingambit's amazing bulk allows it to consistently survive big hits such as Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake, letting it set up a Swords Dance and fire back with +2 Sucker Punch.

  • Iron Head versus Low Kick: Iron Head provides the best all-around power and coverage, allowing Kingambit to better threaten Primarina, Mimikyu, and Mega Floette. Low Kick is less flexible and leaves Kingambit vulnerable to Primarina, but it's the best way to take on opposing Kingambit and has a high chance to OHKO offensive Hydreigon after Stealth Rock damage.

Items

  • Black Glasses: Black Glasses doubles down on making Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave as deadly as possible. When combined with Supreme Overlord, +2 Sucker Punch + Black Glasses will always OHKO offensive Garchomp.

  • Lum Berry: If Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance ahead of time, Lum Berry will prevent Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-W from switching in and completely ruining its momentum.

  • Chople Berry: Chople Berry allows Kingambit to withstand some weaker Fighting-type attacks, such as Close Combat from Aegislash and Scizor and unboosted Body Press from Corviknight. With maximum HP investment, Kingambit also has a high chance to survive Jolly Mega Lopunny's Close Combat and an average chance to survive Timid Mega Gengar's Focus Blast.

Alternate EV Spread

  • 8 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def / 24 Spe with Adamant: This spread maintains enough bulk to almost always survive Adamant Life Orb Mimikyu's +2 Play Rough after Stealth Rock damage as well as Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake from full health. After maximizing Attack, the remaining SPs are invested into Speed, allowing Kingambit to outrun threats such as Mega Clefable with 2 Speed SPs.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Gholdengo threatens Archaludon, Mega Staraptor, Starmie, and Mega Floette. Trick and Good as Gold allow it to punish slow defensive play by locking Pokemon like Hippowdon and Corviknight into one move. It struggles a bit with damage, as it won't OHKO other threats it outspeeds like Mega Delphox, Basculegion-M, Mega Metagross, and Skeledirge without a bit of chip damage first. Gholdengo's Speed tier can also be lackluster at times, meaning Pokemon that can boost their Speed like Mega Gyarados, Mega Charizard X, and Mega Blaziken can take advantage of Gholdengo and position themselves to sweep.

  • Trick: Trick is quite useful against more utility-oriented Archaludon sets by locking them into a move and taking their Sitrus Berry. It can lock bulky Pokemon like Hippowdon, Bellibolt, and Umbreon into their recovery moves or attacks, turning them into setup fodder for Gholdengo's teammates. Trick can also stop dual screen setters like Grimmsnarl by taking its Light Clay and setup sweepers like Kingambit from using Swords Dance.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt provides coverage against Flying- and Water-types, such as Pelipper, Mega Staraptor, Hisuian Samurott, Primarina, Greninja, and Mega Gyarados.

  • Power Gem: Power Gem OHKOes Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona. It also provides Flying-type coverage similarly to Thunderbolt but can hit Mega Dragonite and Fire-types like Mega Charizard X for super effective damage.

  • Timid vs. Modest: With a Timid nature, Gholdengo can outspeed +1 Mega Gyarados, Jolly Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, Jolly Mega Lopunny, and Timid Mega Delphox. Modest Gholdengo's Shadow Ball has a 50% chance to OHKO Mega Metagross without chip damage, and it additionally 2HKOes Garchomp so that Gholdengo doesn't have to be locked into Make It Rain. A Modest nature also enables the OHKO on Choice Scarf Meowscarada with Make It Rain, so it can no longer act as a check.

Other Options

  • Recover: Recover is a viable option even with Trick, as Gholdengo can heal up against targets locked into utility moves like Stealth Rock. This is particularly effective against Archaludon, which Gholdengo generally walls.

  • Dazzling Gleam: Dazzling Gleam can catch Hydreigon switching in off-guard, as it generally beats this set. However, this surprise only works once, as Gholdengo is slower than Choice Scarf Hydreigon and OHKOed by Dark Pulse. Dazzling Gleam also provides coverage against other Dragon- and Dark-types like Hisuian Samurott and Mega Gyarados, though its lower Base Power means Make It Rain and Gholdengo's other coverage moves are usually better options.

Archaludon.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the Regulation M-B metagame! Expect rapid changes as the metagame is still evolving.

Bulky Entry Hazard Setter.description:
• Archaludon is one of the best walls in the entire game thanks to its incredible bulk and Stamina. With access to Stealth Rock, phazing support, and Draco Meteor, Archaludon can efficiently wear down lineups that lack dedicated checks to it.

  • Thunderbolt versus Flash Cannon: Thunderbolt is Archaludon's best complementary move to Draco Meteor for its ability to hit key bulky targets Primarina and Corviknight, which comfortably check Archaludon otherwise, as well as hitting many other Steel-types neutrally.
