Flash Cannon is a more consistent damage source overall, but it doesn't help Archaludon against Steel-types like Corviknight, Scizor, and Aegislash.

  • Roar versus Dragon Tail: Roar is the preferred phazing option for racking up Stealth Rock damage, as Pokemon immune to it are extremely uncommon, and it works through Substitute. Dragon Tail is more generally oppressive by dealing direct damage and phazing at the same time, and it additionally cannot be shut down by Taunt. However, Dragon Tail can make Archaludon struggle against Substitute users and does not work at all on Mega Floette, which can set up on Archaludon and threaten to snowball out of control.

  • Mirror Coat: Archaludon's bulk makes it a viable user of Mirror Coat, which allows it to deal significant damage or completely take out targets such as Primarina and Mega Gengar.

  • Sitrus Berry versus Leftovers: Sitrus Berry's burst recovery is more effective at helping Archaludon survive multiple hits from big attacks, including super effective ones like Garchomp's Earthquake. On the other hand, Leftovers is superior when Archaludon can capitalize long-term on Stamina boosts from favorable defensive matchups against foes such as Meowscarada and Mega Starmie.

Other Options

  • Foul Play: Foul Play gives Archaludon a direct option against difficult physical attackers like Aegislash and Mega Metagross.

  • Rest and Chesto Berry: Restoring Archaludon to full health after receiving several Stamina boosts can completely ruin physically offensive lineups that rely on attrition to beat Archaludon.

SP Spreads

  • All 2HKOs mentioned below factor in Archaludon having a +1 Defense boost from Stamina for the second hit.

  • 32 HP / 23 Def / 11 SpD with Bold: With this spread, Archaludon is guaranteed to avoid the 2HKO from Jolly Basculegion-M's 150-Base Power Last Respects and, when using Sitrus Berry, Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake. Leftover SPs are put into Special Defense.

  • 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpD with Calm: Maximum special bulk investment allows Archaludon to avoid the 2HKO from Timid Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball and Modest Primarina's Moonblast, assuming no Fairy Feather on the latter. This spread works particularly well with Mirror Coat, as Archaludon also has a significant chance to survive +1 Moonblast from offensive Mega Floette.

Pseudo-Focus Sash.description:
• Archaludon can perform consistently as an offensive lead thanks to Sturdy, which lets it take full advantage of its respectable Speed and high-power attacks.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt provides strong overlapping coverage with Draco Meteor, in particular pressuring defensive mainstays Primarina and Corviknight.

  • Flash Cannon versus Steel Beam: Flash Cannon is the safest option for a Steel-type STAB attack and is more than sufficient against the likes of offensive Mimikyu and Glimmora. However, Steel Beam's massive Base Power makes dealing with bulkier threats like Hippowdon much more viable, even if it comes at the cost of survivability.

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere helps Archaludon win the mirror matchup while avoiding Draco Meteor usage, keeping its Special Attack stable and making it less likely to become setup bait. Even specially defensive Archaludon has a high chance to be 2HKOed. Aura Sphere is also the best option for taking on Kingambit.

  • Stealth Rock: The combination of Archaludon's Speed and Sturdy allows it to reliably set Stealth Rock.

  • Roar: Roar can disrupt dangerous setup sweepers like Iron Defense Mega Metagross and Swords Dance Mega Blaziken.

  • Timid versus Modest: Many offensive threats such as Adamant Mimikyu, Jolly Basculegion-M, Jolly Hisuian Samurott, and Jolly Mega Gyarados are at or just below Archaludon's positive-nature Speed tier. As such, a Timid nature is usually preferred. However, the power increase from a Modest nature is still worth considering; for example, it gives Archaludon a decent chance to OHKO offensive Mega Gengar with Draco Meteor.

Other Options

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse is offensive Archaludon's best means of pressuring Aegislash and Gholdengo directly.

  • Mirror Coat: Sturdy allows for more confident Mirror Coat usage, especially against targets like Gholdengo that boost their Special Attack, but it limits the direct offensive nature that this set likes to utilize and is very reliant on Sturdy being active.

Items

  • White Herb: White Herb allows Archaludon to fire off Draco Meteor once without worrying about the subsequent Special Attack drop, giving it incredible burst potential and generally making it less exploitable by setup attackers.

  • Sitrus Berry: Archaludon's defensive typing and stats are so strong naturally that Sitrus Berry can still be worth running on an offensive set. Sitrus Berry will also always activate after using Steel Beam, giving Archaludon an extra health buffer as well as the potential to fire off a second Steel Beam without fainting.

Rain Sweeper.description:
• When paired with a rain setter like Pelipper, Archaludon can build dangerous offensive momentum with Electro Shot.

  • Electro Shot : Thanks to the Special Attack boost, even the first Electro Shot used can be difficult to switch into without an Electric resistance, and it can also OHKO frailer targets like Mega Lucario.

  • Draco Meteor : Electro Shot may be the star of the show, but Draco Meteor is often Archaludon's best option when you're trying to play around Ground-type switch-ins such as Garchomp.

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere provides consistent coverage independent from the weather, pressuring Dark-types like Kingambit and opposing Archaludon.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt is an alternative Electric-type option to use outside of rain, which can be especially relevant for keeping pressure on Mega Charizard Y.

SP Spreads and Items

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: A standard offensive spread for use with Choice Scarf. A Timid nature is mandatory, as Archaludon wants to outrun Choice Scarf Jolly Basculegion-M.

  • 32 HP / 11 Def / 15 SpA / 8 Spe with Modest: Going with a bulkier spread along with a Sitrus Berry sacrifices immediate offensive pressure, but it eases the need for prediction and allows Archaludon more flexibility in and out of rain. Enough Special Attack investment is maintained to guarantee that Electro Shot OHKOes offensive Mega Gyarados, and the Speed investment is enough to outrun fully invested base 60s like Primarina. The remaining SPs go into HP and Defense, giving Archaludon a decent chance of avoiding the 2HKO from Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake after Sitrus Berry healing and a Stamina activiation.

Focus Energy.description:
• By utilizing Focus Energy and Scope Lens for guaranteed critical hits, not only can Archaludon ignore its own Draco Meteor's stat drops, but it can also rip through the defensive boosts of tanky threats like Clefable and its Mega Evolution!

  • Draco Meteor: Draco Meteor can still be used as an upfront burst option prior to using Focus Energy, allowing Archaludon to adapt to what works best in each matchup. This can make Focus Energy + Draco Meteor a nasty surprise for anything trying to set up on a "weakened" Archaludon.

  • Flash Cannon: Flash Cannon is for Fairy-types like Mimikyu and Primarina, which can ignore Draco Meteor. After Archaludon uses Focus Energy, it will always OHKO physically defensive Unaware Clefable.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt is more immediately threatening to Primarina than Flash Cannon, and it also prevents Archaludon from getting walled by Corviknight. While Flash Cannon is much more consistent against Clefable overall, Focus Energy + Thunderbolt can still get the job done on Mega Clefable because of its new typing.

  • Substitute: Substitute can block status moves like Yawn from Hippowdon and Umbreon, giving Archaludon an opportunity to set up Focus Energy safely.

  • Stamina versus Sturdy: The choice between abilities comes down primarily to what SP spread Archaludon is running. If Archaludon is using a bulky spread, it should have Stamina; if it's using a purely offensive spread, Sturdy is preferable.

Other Options

  • Foul Play and Dark Pulse: Even with a Modest nature and a Focus Energy boost, Archaludon cannot reliably 2HKO HP-invested King's Shield Aegislash with Thunderbolt. Foul Play allows Archaludon to always 2HKO physical attacker Aegislash in Shield forme, and it will also always 2HKO special attacker variants after a Focus Energy boost. Dark Pulse is another option that isn't as efficient against physical attacker Aegislash but makes it possible to threaten Gholdengo, which Foul Play can't do.

EV Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 SpA / 2 Spe with Modest: This is a simple bulky attacker spread that lets Archaludon work particularly well against slower cycle and stall teams; it also helps Archaludon respond better to threats that try to set up while using Focus Energy. For example, maximum HP Archaludon avoids the OHKO from Mega Gyarados's +1 Earthquake. Substitute sets appreciate the HP investment as well, since Umbreon's Foul Play will almost never break Substitute in one hit.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest or Timid: Focusing on Speed lets Archaludon outrun variants of Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott that have some Speed investment. A Modest nature gives an unboosted Draco Meteor the best shot of OHKOing specially defensive variants of Garchomp, but a Timid nature will allow Archaludon to outrun Adamant Mimikyu and Speed tie at worst with opposing Archaludon.
